paragraphs: Kent stood before the towering door, looking dazed. One couldn’t tell if he was overwhelmed by the towering sight before him or the fact that he had just died—killed, actually.
"So, I died," Kent muttered, no emotion whatsoever on his face. Perhaps the towering structure was doing all the emoting for him, so he just stood, watching it with a flat expression.
"How disappointing, to think I died without getting laid." Kent smiled slightly. "Truly disappointing, indeed," he added with a sigh.

Then he moved, walking toward the door that seemed to have opened slightly. One might wonder what Kent was doing, but as a movie director who had made many films based on reincarnation and similar themes, he knew walking through the door was the next move for him.

It was as if he had made peace with his situation. Even though he had just died, he wasn’t angry or anything. As the woman had said, he held all his hatred deep within his heart; at a glance, anyone would say he was perhaps the happiest person in the universe.
"Fascinating," the woman said, her expression neutral, though her eyes remained filled with hate.
"Why don’t you step away from the door first so we can have a conversation," she suggested. Kent sighed and moved as she instructed.
"Make it quick, lady. My life has already been hell, so I’d rather continue my journey than spend time with a beautiful woman I can’t have," Kent said, walking forward.
"You don’t seem angry for someone who was just murdered," the woman remarked.
"What’s the point, anyway?" Kent stopped when he was far enough from the door. "I’m all ears, lady."
"Before we go any further, may I know your name?" she asked.

"You already knew I was murdered; what’s stopping you from reading my mind to find out? I don’t mean to be rude, but next time you meet someone, maybe try asking their name instead of reading their thoughts," Kent replied, his tone raised.
Inwardly, though, he wondered why he’d shouted at her. He was always reasonable and never lashed out at anyone, not even at the priest who conducted the burial rites for his parents when they passed.
"It’s the realm you’re in. It’s not your fault," the woman responded, reading his mind again. Kent just sighed and looked at her, waiting for her to continue.

Kent narrowed his gaze at her for a minute and then said,
"Is that supposed to be scary? Because it’s not. In fact, that would be a better existence for me than being born with an amazing body, only to be deprived of everything that should come with it."

"So, Vexthra, if I have to hate something—if I do hate something—then it’s gods and goddesses like you who pretend to care about others. chapters.title: Chapter 4: Planning
paragraphs: Kent gazed at the screen displaying a multitude of skills and techniques—things he’d never imagined could actually exist somewhere in the universe.
He’d done a few fantasy movies, so he was familiar with some of these fictional abilities, but he’d never considered that they could be real.
As he looked through the list, Vexthra turned to him with her usual piercing gaze.

"I promised I’d give you the power to have any woman you desire, and I intend to keep that promise. But before we continue with what I have in store for you, I need to tell you about the world I’ll be sending you to. Your previous world is just a low-level one, with no cultivation."

Kent nodded. He had no intentions of returning there anyway. His parents were gone, and as an only child, he felt no strong ties. As for uncles and cousins, he knew they’d be fine; his assets would be passed on to them once his death was discovered.

"The world I would be sending you to is called Sonox, it is a Medium-level world. And before you ask, worlds are grouped into different levels. The world you came from is a low-level world and as such, low-level worlds don’t have Spiritual Qi to cultivate and grow stronger.
"But aside from that, there is a Medium, High, Immortal, God, Supreme, and Celestial worlds. Based on the naming you should know they each have different power levels"

Kent nodded. He doesn’t need someone telling him a High world would be superior to a low-level world. What troubled him though was the fact that she wasn’t sending him to a high world or even a God world instead of just a Medium world.
"You’re probably wondering why I’m not sending you to a god world, considering I want you to kill a god. It would only be natural to go there instead," Vexthra said rhetorically. Kent nodded.

"That’s because, although I am a goddess, I don’t have the authority to manipulate the laws and send you there. Since you won’t be transmigrating into another person, it would be hard to send you there.
The same is true for an immortal world. The laws are just as strict there, so sending you to those two areas is next to impossible."
"What about a high world?" Kent asked. At least a high world would be a step up from a medium one.

"Although I can work my way into sending you to a high world, it wouldn’t be something you could survive, considering the kind of life I have in mind for you—or more precisely, the kind of power I have in mind for you," Vexthra replied.
Kent raised an eyebrow at that. ’The kind of power she has in mind for me. What kind of power would be that disadvantageous for me?’ Kent wondered.

"It’s simple, actually. You’re doing this so I can help you live the life you never had in your previous one. So tell me, say you went and slept with the wife of a king who is a Spirit King—do you think you could defend yourself?

"Of course, I did promise to make you powerful, but I can’t just make you immortal. What I can do, though, is give you the power to grow stronger. So while going to a high world would make you grow faster, it would also be dangerous.

"And like I said, you’re the only one who can help me now, so I can’t afford to send you into the lion’s den. Even the medium world I have in mind for you is just a few steps away from becoming a high world, so that place is also dangerous.
But I have my reasons for wanting to send you there..."
"Go on," Kent said. He didn’t really care where he went, as long as he could find Nether Caves to stick his rod in; he’d be okay.
"Sonox, as I said, is a medium world. However, it’s not a world for humans alone. It’s a mixed-race world where Humans, Dragons, Elves, Beastkin, and even Demons reside."
"Demons are real?" Kent asked.
"Of course demons are real. I am a demon myself," Vexthra said, watching Kent’s reaction.

’Damn, I wonder how her p*ssy would taste,’ Kent thought, eyeing her with a glint of mischief. Vexthra, hearing his thoughts, reacted inwardly but hid it well—though, of course, the former p*rn director noticed.
Cough!!

"As I was saying, the world of Sonox has different races. I will be sending you to the Human Continent, to a kingdom called Althea. It’s one of the four kingdoms kingdoms with roughly ten cities. However, before you get any ideas, just know that this single kingdom is as large as a continent in the world you came from.
"The strongest there could crush you like an ant, but if you lay low for a few months and diligently use the powers I’ll be giving you, you can start roaming as you see fit."
"Sounds good enough," Kent said, looking more pleased with himself than before.
"Now, let’s talk about how you’re going to approach the task," Vexthra said.

"I already know. You want me to kill the God of Alchemy, so it’s only natural that I become an alchemist. That would be the only way to get close to him and snuff him out, right?" Kent replied with a grin.

"Yes, but I don’t plan on making you just an alchemist. I’ll ensure you have the power to fight like a warrior and concoct pills like a true master. And, of course, you’ll also gain the ability to learn anything much faster," Vexthra said, making sure Kent understood she meant every word.

"So, does that mean I’ll become something of a Grandmaster Alchemist right off the bat?" Kent asked with a smile. Alchemy was one of the professions he explored in his movies, so the thrill of actually having the chance to experience it in real life was enticing.
"No," Vexthra said.
"But you’ll have a legacy with all the necessary knowledge in it. All you’ll have to do is build a foundation, which will make things even easier for you in the future.
"But before you get disappointed, know that once I hand over what I’ve planned for this mission, you’ll see that the task will be just as enjoyable as you can imagine.

"All I ask is that you do well and grow stronger so you can help me. Of course, I won’t have any influence over your life after you leave this place, so you could choose to ignore me and go live your life. However, I hope you won’t do that.

"After all, I’ve been planning this mission for the past two million years," Vexthra said. Had it not been for her nature as the Goddess of Hate and Resentment, Kent would have seen the pain in her eyes. But even without the look, he sensed her pain in her tone.
"I promise I won’t slack off or abandon my mission. You’re giving me a second chance at life; I won’t waste it," Kent said.
Vexthra paused for a moment, just staring into his eyes. Then, she extended her hand, and a small tower appeared.
"What is this?" Kent asked.
"It’s called the Tower of Inheritance, but after hundreds of thousands of years of fine-tuning, it has become something of a sentient tower."
"Like a system?" Kent asked, his fists clenched.
"You could say that."
"YESSS!" he shouted, punching the air.

chapters.title: Chapter 5: The Primordial Chaos Dragon Harem System
paragraphs: Kent stared at the miniature tower with excited eyes. As a movie director who had done some fictional movies, he knew all about "systems"—those enhanced, sentient intelligence in fantasy stories that help cultivators easily walk the path of immortality.

He had worked on movies and TV shows featuring such ideas, and personally, he was intrigued by the concept. So the moment he saw the tower and Vexthra confirmed it was something akin to a system, his excitement soared.
"Relax, Kent," Vexthra said, noticing his growing enthusiasm as he gazed at the miniature tower. "This isn’t the type of system you’re imagining, though it does contain some of what you’ll need."
"What do you mean by that? Is it a system or not?" Kent asked, frowning at her cryptic words.

"It is indeed a system—a one-of-a-kind one, actually. But it’s not exactly what you had in mind. Before you jump to conclusions, let me explain what this is. It will help you understand the nature of this system and the power I’ve prepared for your mission," Vexthra said.
Kent nodded. Although he wasn’t thrilled with the uncertainty, he knew better than to make assumptions too soon. He focused, ready to hear what Vexthra had to say.

"First, you need to understand that this tower is the sole inheritance left by the most powerful being of the Primordial era—the Chaos Dragon. He was the first of his kind, and after him, there was no other Chaos Dragon.
"That being said, the tower itself is a legacy left by this dragon, in the hope of finding someone worthy of carrying on his power. Many tried to locate it, but none were fortunate enough to succeed.

"Now, before you ask how I got it—I didn’t. It was entrusted to me two million years ago. And before you wonder what a legacy is, it’s essentially the entire cultivation of knowledge and power of the Primordial Chaos Dragon, collected and prepared for a successor.

"The reason I said it’s somewhat like a system is that, while the tower can’t directly affect the laws of the world by, say, suppressing someone’s cultivation base or trapping them, it instead grants you the power to do that yourself.
"In other words, without you as the medium, the system—or the tower—is essentially powerless.
"But don’t be discouraged. The Tower is a Celestial-grade item that has been evolving over the past two million years. It holds far more than you could ever ask for.

"Techniques, weapons, treasures—you name it, the Tower has it all. So, while you might have expected a system that would do everything for you, this one will instead empower you to do everything yourself. You’ll gain access to knowledge and resources that cultivators can only dream of.
"So, tell me, Kent, do you want to proceed with the mission?" Vexthra asked after she explained.
"Are you kidding me? Let’s do it. I would have been disappointed to have a system that dictated my entire life," Kent said with a beaming smile. At least he got a say in how things went for him.

"Good. Now, before you carry on, there’s one thing you should know about the Primordial Dragon. He was a bit of a pervert, so inheriting his legacy would make you the successor of a pervert—though a very powerful one, considering you’d be inheriting his bloodline and physique."
"’Pervert’ is such a harsh word, don’t you think, Vexthra? Where I come from, it’s called a ’man of culture,’" Kent smiled, remembering some of the scripts he had written for his movies.
"So, what do I do next?" Kent asked. "I presume this legacy has everything that can help me become an alchemy legend."

"Indeed. But until you manage to inherit it, you’ll never be able to use it," Vexthra said, looking at Kent with a worried expression... though, with her eyes full of hatred, it was hard to tell if it was worry or just pure hate.
"How do I do that?" Kent asked.
"Just drop your blood on it, and it will activate if you are worthy," Vexthra said.
Kent nodded, bit the tip of his index finger, and, when blood appeared, he gently dropped it on the tower. As soon as the blood landed, the room they were in began to shake.
"What is happening?" Kent asked in a panicked tone.
The air swirling around him was full of hatred and resentment making the situation even more alarming.
He felt fear.
But when he saw the frown on Vexthra’s face, he grew even more worried. Even the goddess looked concerned. A mere mortal, what is expected of him?
Meanwhile, in the Celestial realm, in a large room, on a large bed, a handsome man with dark gray hair and a well-refined body opened his eyes surrounded by naked beauties of various races.
Humans, demons, elves, orcs, dragons—a variety of women lay passed out on the bed. The man suddenly turned in a certain direction.
"Looks like he has finally arrived," he smiled, handsomely yet with a hint of perversion.

"Very well, let’s see whether you can handle this small task. If you are anything like before, it should be simple enough." He extended his hand, and a small orb of light flew from it into the far distance.
He smirked, then turned back to a cute pink nipple. With a quick motion, his lips wrapped around it. His hand drifted toward the nether region of a succubus, instantly filling the room with moans.

Back in the Realm of Hatred and Resentment, Kent and Vexthra were anxiously waiting when, suddenly, the shaking stopped. As soon as it did, the tower shrank and entered Kent’s forehead. His eyes rolled back, sending him into an unconscious state.
It happened so fast that before Vexthra could react, he was already passed out.
A while later, he woke up. However, the moment he opened his eyes, a message flashed before him:
[Welcome to the Primordial Chaos Dragon Tower, where Your Passion and Pleasure is our Priority.]
[You are about to inherit the legacy of the Primordial Chaos Dragon. But to unlock, you must first complete a Quest.]
[Quest: Pleasure the Goddess of Hatred and Resentment. You must make her smile for the first time in 3.6 million years to pass this quest. ]
[Rewards:]
- Primordial Chaos Dragon Legacy
- Primordial Alchemy Records
- Primordial Genesis Sword Art
- Primordial Chaos Dragon Harem System

"You better, or else I will come down there and kick your ass," Vexthra’s smile bloomed.
Kent wrapped his arm around her waist and pulled her closer.
"I know you said it will take years for us to meet again, but I have a feeling we will be seeing each other sooner than you think.
That being said, read all the books I recommended and do them as a mortal.
If you are not lazy like me, it will take you a couple of years to finish them all.
By then, I will have figured out a way for us to meet again," Kent said, and Vexthra nodded like a baby.
He planted a kiss on her lips.
"Now send me on my way.
There are other ladies out there waiting for my nine-inch dragon," Kent laughed.
Vexthra smiled slightly and then pressed her finger against his forehead.
Kent felt an energy move through his body, and then he blacked out.

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Disciple of a Shameless Alchemist
paragraphs: Inside a makeshift apartment, a man could be seen sitting behind a flameless cauldron, looking rather happy for obvious reasons. He appeared to have achieved something extraordinary, but if one looked closely, one could tell he was dead.
Yes... the dude is dead. This man is called James Hogan; he is an alchemist in Caprath City, one of the major cities in the Althea Kingdom. In Caprath City, James is known as the shameless alchemist.
He is brilliant but incredibly shameless. No matter the situation he finds himself in, he always has a way out. He had been like that for many years until, finally, his mischief caught up with him.
In a few days, he would be selected among a few alchemists to go and see if they could cure the sick daughter of a merchant.

James, who might have gotten a hint of this, was eager to get what he wanted. The merchant would promise that whoever was able to cure his daughter would get to marry her. Though nobody knew, James—sneaky as ever—managed to get wind of it.

And because of this, he started preparing for the event. However, due to his haste and eagerness to please, he overexerted himself and died before he could finish concocting the sex-enhancement pill he had planned to use.
One could say he died planning to make someone’s daughter beg her for more. He planned to go down on her hard.
He looked happy when he died, meaning he had succeeded. Inside the cauldron, one could see the pill sitting peacefully in there.
Suddenly, the space cracked inside the room, and a young man with whitish-purple hair fell out. Kent landed on the floor just a few meters from James Hogan. He passed out.
It took a few hours, but gradually, he opened his eyes, taking in the new environment he had been thrown into. After adjusting his vision for a few moments, he sighed and then stood up.
His gaze immediately locked onto James, and then, like a flood, he sensed a load of memories pour into his mind.

"James Hogan, huh... So that was the backstory she had prepared for me," Kent said, shaking his head. He received the memories of James, which meant he now knew a lot about the city and kingdom he had been transported to.
"I guess she did plan everything..." Kent sighed as he walked closer to James. However, before he could approach, messages started ringing in his mind.
"Here we go," he sighed again, sitting down beside the dead James, who held a smile on his face even in his last moments.
Kent’s attention immediately focused on the messages that had appeared, neatly arranged by the Tower.
[Congratulations on completing your first quest by making the Goddess of Hate and Resentment smile.]
[Rewards received. You can take out the rewards by accessing your Tower storage. Current items in storage: Primordial Alchemy Records, Primordial Genesis Sword Art, Infinity Cultivation Art.]
[You have already received the Primordial Chaos Dragon Legacy and Unlocked Primordial Chaos Dragon Harem System.]
[Congratulations on completing your second quest. You have received 10,000 Tower Points. These points can be used to purchase items from the Tower Store.]
[The store will be unlocked when you break through to the Root Grandmaster stage.]
"Hmm, I guess the things I wrote in my movies aren’t far-fetched," Kent muttered, then returned to the messages. He had completed three quests, after all.
[Congratulations on completing your third quest. You have received 50,000 Tower Points and two unique SSS-Rank Skills.]

"SSS-Rank skills—that’s wild. I wonder what they are," Kent thought, wanting to check them immediately, but the next set of messages caught his attention. He set the skills aside for now and focused on the other messages.
[Congratulations on adding the first member to your Harem. You have unlocked some features and benefits.]
[Features]
- Telepathy: You can telepathically communicate with the members of your harem. This feature also extends to your harem members; they can communicate with you and among themselves.
- Bestow: You can bestow skills and techniques to your harem members. At your current level, you can bestow only one skill. As you level up, you will be able to add more.

- Take: Besides the random skill that is obtained after adding a member to your harem, you can also access their skill page and take two more skills. This number will increase as you continue to level up.
[Note: More features will be added as you rise in ranks.]
[Benefits]
- Your soul grows stronger as you add more members to your harem. This benefit arises from the link formed between you and your partners.
- You earn part of the spiritual qi absorbed by your harem members as they cultivate.
"Well, that’s great, I guess," Kent smiled. "Does this mean my soul strength has become stronger now that Vexthra is in my harem?"
"Scratch that, telepathy—does it mean I can talk to her now? How does it work, Tower?" Kent asked, eager to see if he could reach his sugar goddess.

[The Master can indeed contact Goddess Vexthra, but due to the realm difference, the connection can hold for only 5 minutes every 100 days. However, as the Master ascends to higher realms, this connection will last much longer.]
"That’s awesome. Can I contact her now? If so, how?" Kent asked again.
[Yes... You must first focus on the connection formed between you. Just concentrate, and you will sense it.]
Kent closed his eyes and focused. Almost instantly, he tapped into the connection, making his smile bloom.
Somewhere in the Realm of Hatred and Resentment.

Vexthra, who was sitting on her bed reading a novel, suddenly felt a sudden jolt coming from below her belly. She looked down, only to see a tower tattoo appear there. It was a puzzling sight, but before she could wonder what was happening, a voice entered her mind, making her eyes widen.
<My sugar goddess, can you hear me?>
"Kent..." Vexthra called out.
<The one and only. Told you it wouldn’t be long before hear from me,> Kent bragged.
"How is this possible? You are in the Mortal Realm, and I am in the God Realm. This shouldn’t be possible. How are you contacting me?" Vexthra asked.
<I have a tower,> Kent replied.

<By the way, we can only talk for five minutes every 100 days. So I just wanted to check whether it works, and it does, so for the next 100 days, we can talk for five minutes. We’ve already spent 40 seconds, so I’ll be hanging up now.
And hey, thanks for sending me to a dead alchemist, very creative> Kent added smiling.
"You needed a backstory, so I gave you one. The unknown disciple of a dead alchemist is the perfect backstory," Vexthra said with a smile.
<I’ll talk to you later, Vex. For now, let me settle down and get my affairs in order. These five minutes can’t be wasted... Bye.>
Kent cut the connection, leaving a smile on Vexthra’s face. Kent had left her not long ago, but she was already starting to miss him.

One might think that for someone who had lived for millions of years, missing someone would be the last thing on her mind. But, well, she was a different person now, thanks to Kent bringing life back into her lifeless eyes.
Back in the makeshift apartment in Sonox, Kent returned to the messages. Most were about what to do next to unlock the towers. When he was done with them, he accessed the SSS-ranked skills.

chapters.title: Chapter 13: Divine Pervert Touch, an SSS-Ranked Skill
paragraphs: When Kent received the third quest, the rewards included 50,000 Tower Points and two hidden rewards. At the time, he had been too thrilled to get intimate with Vexthra, so he hadn’t paid much attention to it.
However, his focus sharpened now that he was about to start his quest—the grand mission of rising through the ranks as an alchemist to get close to the Alchemy God and take him out.

Kent’s sole purpose now was to grow stronger and, well, enjoy as much pleasure as he could along the way. After all, the primary reason he had accepted this mission was the chance to finally experience what sexual pleasure feels like.

With that in mind, Kent never truly expected much from the hidden rewards. To his surprise, he received two SSS-Rank skills instead of something minor. when he began to read the first one, he could hardly believe his eyes.
[Skill Name: Divine Pervert Touch]
[Grade/Rank: SSS]
[Effects]
Arousal Touch - With intent, when you touch a woman, there is a 100% chance of arousing her. If she craves you, a simple touch can even bring her to a climax.

Demon Touch - With intent, when you touch or strike a male, they will experience pain amplified 1000 times. The effect depends on your imagination, so even a light touch can transform them into what you want them to experience. Just don’t go overboard... lol.

"Damn, that’s something," Kent murmured, smiling as he imagined the possibilities of this skill. On the bright side, he could literally turn any woman on with just a touch. Of course, it would require genuine intent, but that single touch could send her to the peak of pleasure.
"At this rate, I’m on track to becoming a better massage artist than an alchemist," Kent laughed out loud, his voice echoing like a maniac.

The skill had everything he could wish for, a perfect tool for his second chance at life—a chance meant to reward him with all the pleasures he’d been deprived of in his previous 34 years of existence.
"Now with the demon touch, just a single slap can induce this much pain. Damn, that’s just too awesome," Kent grinned. "At this rate, I won’t even need to raise my sword."

"Although the effect is vague, I know there’s something sinister about this skill. I guess I should integrate into society soon so I can practice on some unlucky bastards," Kent smiled and then moved to the next SSS-rank skill.
"Well, this is more—how should I put it?" Kent was taken aback again by the next skill.
[Skill Name: 10,000 Ways of Pleasure Manual]
[Grade/Rank: SSS]
[Effects]
- With blood pumping through your d*ck, there is no p*ssy you can’t pleasure. You now have all 10,000 different styles to pleasure any woman, regardless of her race.
- Be it Human, Elf, Dragon, Demon, or Angel—as long as they have p*ssy, you can pleasure them without fear of falling short. Good luck.

"Well, that took a sharper turn than I expected." Kent smiled, re-reading the descriptions. It just looked bizarre that, aside from the pervert touch, he now had more than a hundred ways to pleasure a woman.
"At this rate, I’ll be swimming in pussy before I know it. But that’s a good thing for me, at least. After all, I deserve the best of the best." He chooses to convince himself

Kent knew he was in for a thrill, considering he hadn’t even started his journey but had already received some of the best skills anyone could ask for. With 10,000 ways to pleasure any woman, who in their right mind wouldn’t be happy about that?

That being said, he still hadn’t checked the other rewards he’d received from the first quest. The tower had already told him they came in the form of technique books, so all he had to do was take them out and touch them to his forehead to learn them.
The sword technique manual, the alchemy manual, and his cultivation technique. But first, he accessed his status page.
[Status]+[Harem]+[Alchemy]+[Bloodline Traits & Skills]

Age: 18
Bloodline: Primordial Chaos Dragon
Class: Alchemist (Locked)
SubClass: Swordsman (Locked)
Cultivation: Root Awakening - Lvl 1/9
Physical Strenght: 20
Physical Agility: 20
Physical Stamina: 50
Spiritual Strenght: 200
Mental Strength: 120
[Tower Points: 60,000]
[Attribute Points: 10]
[Skill Upgrade Points: 0]
Skills and Techniques:
[Divine Pervert Touch (Active - SSS) | 10,000 Ways Of Pleasure Manual (Active - SSS) | Sword Intent (Passive - B) | Aura of Hatred and Resentment (Passive - SS) ]
"Hmm, looks like I have a lot to do."
"I’ll need to use that technique to raise my cultivation base since Vexthra has limited it in other not to have a shaky foundation," Kent said, then retrieved the techniques from the tower storage.
"First, though—Tower, what is an Attribute Point, and why are the Class and Subclass locked?" Kent asked.
[The Attribute Points are for increasing the stats of your strength, speed, stamina, mind, and spirit. You will receive them as you level up and break through to higher stages.
As for your class and subclass, you first have to learn the techniques associated with them to unlock them. You currently have them all in your tower storage.]

"Right," Kent reached into the tower storage and retrieved the three books. He could literally see into this storage, like looking through a portal. It was bizarre in a way, but he knew it was due to the tower he had inherited.
"My cultivation is important—let me handle that first," Kent said before picking up the Primordial Infinity Cultivation Art.
Only its name was on the cover, and inside, there were only complex diagrams. But since the tower had told him to touch it to his forehead, he did.
The book burst into sparkles and entered his forehead. As soon as the book disappeared, a message from the tower appeared.
[Congratulations on learning a Celestial Grade Cultivation technique.]
[Ding! Your cultivation technique has merged with your bloodline. Primordial Infinity Dragon Art formed.]
[Ding! Your cultivation speed has increased by 4000%.]
"That is unexpected but welcome," Kent said, before closing his eyes and beginning to cultivate the technique that had appeared in his mind.
A few seconds later, he leveled up. The tower message appeared immediately, notifying him that he had earned 10 Attribute Points and an additional 5 points added to each of his attributes.
A minute later, he leveled up again. Soon, he began leveling up quickly until he reached level 9. As he had anticipated, he immediately broke through.

But it didn’t stop there; he continued leveling up and soon reached level 3 before the process halted. Vexthra had already mentioned he might break through, but reaching level 3 was beyond his expectations.

In the end, with the breakthrough to the Root Blossom stage, he received 20 points which were added to all attributes, and an additional 50 points added to his reserve, on top of all the points he had already accumulated. His status page appeared just as he had hoped, bringing a satisfied smile to his face.

Physical Strenght: 95
Physical Agility: 95
Physical Stamina: 125

Mental Strength: 195

"Next up, alchemy. I need to know a few things before the messengers from that merchant family arrive. After all, with the master dead, the disciple will have to step in," Kent said, glancing at James Hogan’s dead body beside him.

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Alchemy Genius
paragraphs: Kent took the next book, titled [Primordial Alchemy Records,] and opened it as he had with the cultivation technique. However, unlike the cultivation technique, which contained complex diagrams, this one was filled with text.
The title reads:
"The Art of Alchemy, by Pill Celestial Kevin Sage," Kent read aloud from the first page. He quickly flipped to the second page, where more lines of text appeared.

"This is the manual left behind by the first and only Pill Celestial to ever walk the face of the universe. Inside contains the complete knowledge from his journey from Pill Novice to Pill Celestial. Whoever comes into possession of this manual, if they are worthy, will become an existence capable of revolutionizing the world of alchemy once more.
Good luck, and remember this: a pill is not a pill if it is not 100% pure."
"That’s actually sweet. I wonder who this great figure was like," Kent said, gently tapping the book against his forehead. As with the cultivation manual, it disintegrated and entered his forehead.
"What the hell is..." Kent hadn’t even finished his sentence before he fell backward and passed out.
A few minutes after he passed out, a flame tattoo appeared on his forehead for a few seconds, then vanished. A while later, a thunderbolt tattoo also appeared and disappeared after a few seconds.
He lay there for many hours until, finally, after a full day, he woke up, feeling his head throbbing from the ordeal that had overwhelmed him.
The first thing he noticed, however, was the messages that appeared before his eyes from the Tower.
[Congratulations on learning the Primordial Alchemy Records. Your Alchemy Class has been unlocked. You can now practice alchemy.]

[You have learned the entirety of the Primordial Alchemy Records; however, due to your insignificant level in alchemy, you only have access to the first record - The Pill Novice Primordial Alchemy Records.]

[It contains knowledge on the basics of how to concoct pills and some pill recipes you can try your hand at. Also, you have access to some of the best pill-refining and Flame control techniques in the Primordial Alchemy Records.]

[ You have received a unique Pill Flame Nine Colored Chaos Flame. Now, its strength is that of an Earth-Grade Pill Flame and only the Blue Void Flame has been unlocked. As you unlock more records, your pill flame will also increase in grades]
[To qualify for the next record, you must first succeed in concocting 120 different Tier 0 Pills with 100% purity.]
"That’s a lot to take in, but at least I have something to work with now," Kent said after a while, making sure his headache had subsided.

"The question now is, where the hell am I going to get ingredients from?" Kent sighed. He was new to this world, and although he would love to brag, the master he should be proud of was, unfortunately, quite broke.
He knew this because he currently had his master’s memories.
"Oh, Master isn’t stingy for nothing. He actually has some ingredients in his spatial ring," Kent muttered, reaching for his left hand and sliding the ring off his finger.
Since he had his master’s memories, he knew how to access them.
"Great! With this, I have a chance at concocting a Tier 0 Qi Gathering Pill," Kent said, sounding like an experienced alchemist. This surprised him slightly, so he asked the Tower.
"Tower, why do I sound like I’m some kind of alchemy genius?"

[Master has learned the Primordial Alchemy Records and currently has access to the first record. This means you now know all the basics of alchemy contained within the records. The only thing left is practice.]
"I see," Kent smiled, then walked over to the cauldron and picked up the Tier 1 pill with 50% purity from inside.

"A sex-enhancement pill, huh? Looks like Master was really preparing for this merchant’s unknown daughter. I guess it’s up to me now, but this pill is just too pitiful." Kent crushed the pill, turning it into powder.
He gazed at the lifeless, smiling face of James Hogan and sighed. "I’ll bury you later, Master. For now, watch how your unknown disciple concocts pills."
Kent retrieved the first batch of ingredients, and with a flick of his hand, a blue flame appeared.
"Tower, can you tell me more about this Unique Flame? The records seem to lack that knowledge." Kent asked. He now has Nine different flames but he only has access to one, the Blue Void flame.
If he unlocks more records, the rest will also be unlocked.
[Certainly, Master,] the Tower responded.

[A Unique Flame is a rare, mystical fire. It is found only in special places across the universe. These flames have extraordinary qualities and are difficult to control. Each Unique Flame has its own attributes and strengths. Some can heal, while others can burn through anything, even metal or stone.]
Kent’s eyes widened. "So, this flame is powerful?"

[Yes, Master. This is the Blue Void Flame. It’s a flame known for its purity and control. Alchemists treasure it because it can refine pills with greater precision. It burns steadily, helping you to achieve high purity in your concoctions.]
Kent held out his hand, watching the blue flame flicker and dance. "So, this flame will help me refine pills better?"
[Correct. The Blue Void Flame will give you an edge. With it, you can refine pills faster and with better quality. It’s one of the best flames for an alchemist of your level.]
Kent nodded, feeling a surge of confidence.
"Perfect. Then let’s start with the Qi Gathering Pill." He gathered the ingredients and focused on the flame, watching it dance in his palm. It felt nostalgic in some way.
’This feeling...’ Kent thought, but he didn’t dwell on it. Instead, he quickly followed the knowledge he had acquired from the Primordial Alchemy Records and began heating the cauldron.
"This feels too natural like I was born to control the flame," Kent said, a small smile tugging at his lips. A while later, he dimmed the cauldron was hot enough so he tossed in the first ingredient.

"So this is the feeling. Even with such a thick body, I can see inside the cauldron" Kent muttered as he controlled the pill flame to begin burning and extracting the medicinal essence from the ingredient.
"Easy enough" A few minutes later he tossed in the second one.
Then before long, the third one entered. Kent could tell the more ingredients he added, the more difficult it began to feel, but also the more he understood some things.
Kent knew he had all the knowledge he needed; it was just a matter of making sure his muscles could keep up with what his mind understood.
Five minutes later, the last of the 12 ingredients were burned, and their essences were fully extracted. Using a condensing technique, he began to form the pill.
"Now is when I burn impurities," Kent said as he continued shaping the pill, focusing on removing any impurities as he went.
"I’m a natural," he praised himself with a grin.
[Master is indeed an Alchemy Genius,] the Tower responded, making Kent’s smile widen.
"I knew I was going to like you, Tower. You recognize talent," Kent bragged. Just then, a soft *poof* sounded from the cauldron, followed by a wisp of dark smoke.
He opened the cauldron and saw a dark, misshapen pill inside. Quickly, he picked it out to examine it.
The pill was rough and uneven, with a dull color. Its energy felt weak, almost lifeless. He sighed, realizing the truth.
"It’s terrible," he muttered, shaking his head. "Barely any power in it."
The Tower’s message appeared before him.
[You have successfully concocted a Qi Gathering Pill. Grade: Tier 0, Quality: Poor. Purity: 12%.]
Kent laughed.

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Shocking Progress After Second Trial
paragraphs: After burning his first pill, Kent didn’t immediately begin his second concoction. He sat down and examined the pill for a few more minutes before putting it away in the space ring he had taken from his unofficial master.
Then he turned to face the dead body of his shameless master.
"Let me bury you, master," Kent said, walking toward another room. A few seconds later, he returned with a cloth and wrapped James in it.
He carried him outside and dug a hole. Gently, he placed James in the hole and stood over him with a blank expression. He just couldn’t let the dead sit like that for long.
He tried to say a few words, but everything he thought of felt strange.
He was currently relying on James’ memories, so it felt odd. Nonetheless, he proceeded to say a few words.

"I know we haven’t officially met, but in this life, you are my master. So know that this disciple will fulfill your dream. If this mysterious daughter of the merchant is worth dying for, then I will be sure to make her remember you while I drill her.
It’s only natural for a disciple to make his master proud."
With that, he covered him and walked away.
However, He didn’t immediately return to the house. Instead, he walked forward for a while until he reached the peak of a small mountain.

"Though he died a perverted Alchemist, Master sure knows how to pick his dwelling," Kent said, admiring the scenery before him. There were tall trees, their branches twisting and leaves forming a soothing and harmonious environment.
"The air is clean and nourishing; clearly, global warming is not a thing here," Kent said, sighing.
Back on Earth, just breathing carries a high risk of making one sick. The air was poisonous due to all the toxins being released into the atmosphere. But here is different.
"I guess once I grow strong enough, I’ll go back and set some people straight—and kill a few," Kent grinned, then spent the afternoon there before heading back to the house.

When he returned back to the apartment, He didn’t get down to business right away; instead, he started practicing flame control using the empty cauldron. The Tower had said it was all in the flame control, so he wanted to master that before trying again.
After all, he had already wasted the first of the three portions of ingredients he had, so trial and error was not something he could afford at the moment.

He was broke. His master had wasted all his money on a Sex Enhancement pill recipe, so he would first need to concoct the pill to a decent purity and then sell it when he had the chance to travel to Caprath City. He might do that when the merchant’s soldiers came to pick him up in his master’s stead.

Caprath City was one of the nine cities in the Althea Kingdom. It wasn’t the strongest or the largest, but it was known for great commerce. If what his master heard was true, he would be headed there soon.
According to his master’s memories, a Tier 0 pill with 40% purity could sell for as much as 100 gold coins, equivalent to a single spirit stone.

Kent knew from James’ memories that the highest Tier 0 pill to have appeared in the city was a 94% pure pill from the Divine Palace Sect. It was a Martial and Alchemy sect, renowned for having some of the best alchemists in the Kingdom due to their rigorous training.

It was hard to get in, but Kent knew that was somewhere he would want to be if he wanted to achieve his goal—getting many Beauties. But first, he had to prove to himself whether he had what it took to concoct a good pill.
"A pill is not a pill if it is not 100% pure," Kent muttered. "I guess I have to prove to these records that I have what it takes to be the next Pill Celestial," he declared.
[You may be shooting too far this time, Master, but thumbs up on the confidence,] the Tower said, making Kent want to smack it silly.
"Whose side are you on?" Kent said.
[Yours, of course, Master. But I just want you to stick to your level for now.] The Tower was mocking him at this point, but Kent didn’t mind it anymore.

He took out the next set of ingredients and decided to try concocting the pill again. He would prove to the Tower that he had what it took. After all, it would be the one grading the pill once it was done.
Kent set up his ingredients carefully, his hands steady as he worked. This time, he paid closer attention to each step, recalling the knowledge he had absorbed from the Primordial Alchemy records.
No mistakes this time...
He adjusted the flame control, keeping it steady and consistent, making sure not to let it flare or dim too quickly. Every second counted.

He heated the cauldron slowly, allowing the ingredients to break down smoothly. Last time, he’d rushed this step, causing some ingredients to burn and ruin the concoction. Now, he took his time, letting each herb release its essence fully.

As the mixture started to blend, he stirred gently, mindful of the balance. Too much force could disrupt the harmony within the cauldron. He kept his focus sharp, watching for any signs of instability in the pill’s formation.
Midway through, he realized he’d made some improvements. His flame control was steadier, and he managed the heat with more precision.
The essence extraction, refining, and condensing were much sturdier this time. He was also able to handle the impurity removal great this time too.

Slowly, a faint aroma began to rise from the cauldron. The scent was clear and refreshing—a sign of purity. Kent smiled, knowing he was close. He adjusted the flame one last time, lowering it gently as the pill took form, its surface smooth and without any visible flaws.
Finally, the pill settled, solidifying with a faint glow after 50 minutes of concocting. Kent retrieved it from the cauldron, examining it closely. It wasn’t perfect, but it was better—much better.
The Tower’s voice echoed in his mind.
[Congratulations, Master. That’s a 75% pure pill. A commendable improvement.]
Kent grinned, feeling a surge of satisfaction. He had done it this time.
With one last look at the pill, he placed it carefully into his space ring.

He went back to the process again. He would be able to sell this for a few more gold coins. But he wasn’t satisfied with just the money; for some reason, he hated the idea of depending on an impure pill to earn money.
He felt he needed to do better. Much, much better. So he spent many more hours practicing the flame control arts until he was finally satisfied with the outcome.
He began concocting a new pill, and this time, after 45 minutes, he achieved a good result. A much better result considering he hadn’t been an alchemist for long.
[You have successfully concocted a Qi Gathering Pill. Grade: Tier 0, Quality: Excellent. Purity: 91%.]
He only rested for a few hours before deciding to tackle his next task: unlocking the swordsman subclass. What followed, though, was rather shocking...

chapters.title: Chapter 16: A Genius with the Sword
paragraphs: The first quest granted him five rewards, each one exactly what he wanted. The first was the Harem system, which allowed him to establish a direct line of contact with someone in the god realm—even if it was only for 5 minutes every 100 days.
Nobody else could claim to have such a powerful system that made them so overpowered. Now, he could consult a god without breaking any laws.
But if that wasn’t enough, he also received an incredible cultivation technique. After cultivating it for just a few minutes, he realized it was exactly what he needed to grow stronger.
Initially, Kent had only been cultivating because Vexthra, the goddess of hate and resentment, told him to in order to build a stronger foundation.

However, after the Primordial Infinity Cultivation Art merged with his Primordial Chaos Dragon bloodline, he no longer needed to meticulously build his foundation as he leveled up, unlike everyone else.
His bloodline, coupled with the fact that he now possessed a dragon physique—even if he couldn’t transform yet—allowed him to maintain a stable foundation as he leveled up and broke through.
Currently, his speed was boosted, and though he knew it would take some time to reach the next cultivation stage, he could do so without worrying about bottlenecks or an unstable foundation.
Finding out something like that, Kent wanted to sit down and cultivate until he reached the Root Master stage before setting out to begin his journey.

However, the Tower advised him to let go of that idea, explaining that if he didn’t unlock his swordsmanship class early, he would struggle to do so as he grew stronger without a stable foundation in swordsmanship.
This, of course, felt like a setback—until he unlocked the swordsmanship class and realized he had nearly made a huge mistake.

"Tower, with the Aura of Hatred and Resentment passive skill, I can literally suppress those a realm or two above me. I feel like raising my cultivation base now is the right move," Kent said to the Tower, but its response made him reconsider.

[ Right now, your body is like hot metal, ready for molding. The stronger you become, the tougher it becomes, so while you may think having a high cultivation base is beneficial—and it is—you will later find that you won’t be able to make much progress in your swordsmanship if you don’t drill the basics into your bones now. ]

"Fine, but the moment I master the sword, I won’t hold back from breaking through much faster," Kent said. Perhaps his imagination, shaped by his time on Earth, still clouded his understanding of cultivation, but in a way, that was endearing. After all, he just needed women to have sex with and he will grow stronger.
"Then again, if I have sword skills, I can roam the kingdom and attract beauties who would help me cultivate even faster." Kent grinned. "I’d say it’s a win-win situation for me either way."
He retrieved the Primordial Genesis Sword Art, which, like the Primordial Alchemy Records, contained some writings.

"The Genesis, the beginning of it all. I have chosen to walk the path of the sword, and for billions of years, I have followed it. I started as a Sword Novice until I attained the infamous title ’One with the Sword.’
The path is difficult and deadly, but it is meant for those bold enough to carve their destiny and become the next sword legends.
I created many techniques, included in this manual, but they are sealed and will unlock gradually as you walk the path of the sword.
There are different ways to walk the path of the sword. If you are destined, you will inherit one of the best paths; if not, you might want to lay down your sword and pursue a different calling.
Remember, a sword is only a weapon when wielded by a swordsman. Good luck"

"Poetic but sweet," Kent murmured. For some reason, those words felt strangely familiar. He couldn’t quite place why, but with the manual in hand, he quickly pressed it to his forehead, and it dispersed into his body.
This time, he didn’t pass out. Instead, a message appeared.
[You have read the Primordial Genesis Sword Art. The manual is analyzing your potential to inherit the Sword Tower...]
Kent stood there, staring at the message for a full minute until a notification that nearly made him curse his entire existence appeared.
[Requirements met. Root Blossom Cultivation Base: Check, Sword Intent: Check, Sword Aura: Check, Age Between 16 - 20: Check]
[Congratulations, you have inherited the Sword Tower.]
[Unfortunately, your mastery over the sword is pitifully low, so you cannot access the Sword Tower.]
[Congratulations, you have received the first form of the Primordial Genesis Sword Art: Sword Mind.]
[You must become a Grandmaster Swordsman to unlock the Sword Tower.]
[Current Rank: Novice]

"Wow, that was close," Kent said, breaking into a cold sweat. If he had continued pushing his cultivation base forward instead of following the tower’s instructions, his entire mission would have been for nothing.
"Thank you for stopping me, Tower," Kent said, sincerely grateful he hadn’t been stubborn and had actually listened to reason.
[I am here to serve the Master,] the Tower replied, making Kent calm down a bit.

He then accessed the only thing he had asked for access to: the Sword Mind. He hadn’t really given it much thought, but after seeing the messages, he knew that if he wanted this mission to go well, he would have to listen to the tower.
After all, Vexthra did say it wouldn’t do everything for him but would instead make it easier for him to learn and do things himself.
"Tower, pull up the Sword Mind technique," Kent instructed.
[Status] + [Harem] + [Alchemy] + [Swordsmanship] + [Bloodline Traits & Skills]
[Sword Tower: Inactive]
- You must first become a Grandmaster Swordsman to unlock the tower.
Note: The basics of swordsmanship require you to become familiar with your Sword Qi and Sword Intent.
Skills and Techniques:
[Sword Aura: B Rank]
- Sword Aura/Qi is a unique energy that envelops your sword, allowing you to unleash powerful strikes. Mastery will require you to understand the sword through the Sword Mind technique.
[Sword Intent: A Rank]
- You have manifested the intent of Hatred and Resentment. Mastery of the sword will strengthen your will, allowing you to channel the will of Hatred and Resentment through the sword.
[Sword Mind]
- The first step to walking the path of absolute swordsmanship. This requires you to train the sword using your mind as the training ground.
"This ’Sword Mind’ sounds rather vague," Kent said, reading the message. He had expected something grand, but this?
[The master wouldn’t know until he tries,] the tower responded, in support of the description.

"Fine," Kent said, taking out a sword from the space ring he had taken from his late master. He had anticipated many things, but he hadn’t expected that the moment the sword appeared in his hand, he would feel this intimate connection with it.
[To practice, simply put the sword down and start staring at it as you recite the mantra in your mind.]
Kent obeyed, setting the sword down. Then he focused on it and began reciting the mantra in his mind.

Kent stared at the sword, his gaze fixed and unbroken. The blade shimmered faintly under his focus, as though it sensed his intent. He continued to chant the mantra silently, his mind slowly aligning with the sword.
A strange sensation crept into his consciousness. The world around him faded, leaving only the sword and his thoughts.
He felt a pulse, like a heartbeat, echoing from the blade itself. With each silent chant, the pulse grew stronger, resonating with his own heartbeat.
Images began to flash through his mind—scenes of fierce battles, warriors locked in deadly combat, each wielding swords that radiated with intense intents.
He could feel their intent, their determination, their rage. All of it surged into him, filling him with a raw, untamed power.
Then, something shifted. The energy surrounding the sword flowed into Kent, spreading through his limbs and settling deep within his chest.
His mind sharpened, his senses more acute than ever before. He could almost feel the blade’s sharpness in his own bones.
As Kent continued to focus, clarity filled his mind like a river flowing freely. This was the beginning of Sword Mind—the power to connect with the sword’s essence, beyond its physical form.

In this moment, he was forging its spirit with his own thoughts, crafting a clarity that would be essential on his path. To truly master it, he would need to understand the sword’s ultimate intent—the idea that all swordsmen chased after.
Hours passed, but he did not falter. His body and mind remained locked into the sword’s purpose, sharpening the hateful intent that surrounded him.
Time blurred. He was no longer aware of his surroundings, only the intense, pulsing focus between him and the blade.
A full day went by, yet he continued. The technique came to him naturally, as if his very soul resonated with the sword’s intent.
For the first attempt, he was progressing faster than anyone might have expected. Perhaps he was a sword genius—already wielding both Sword Aura and Sword Intent as if he’d trained for years.
Four days later, he finally opened his eyes.
The sword before him glowed with a faint blue aura, flickering like a gentle flame. As he stared at it, a message appeared before him.
[Congratulations, Master. Your understanding of the sword grows stronger. Current Progress: 45%.]
’I love the sword too?’ Kent thought with a grin.

chapters.title: Chapter 17: Getting summoned
paragraphs: Myrathis is the continent of humans. In Sonox, there are many races, and one of them is the humans. They have four powerful kingdoms, among which Caprath is one of the cities in the Althea Kingdom, ruled by the Althea family.

In Caprath City, although not the capital of Althea Kingdom, there are still some of the most powerful people and businesses. There are also many merchant families, of which the Alderford family is one of the leading merchant families.

They have many businesses and auction houses, and they offer various services regardless of what you need. They thrive in the world of commerce. John Alderford, the head of the Alderford merchant family, has many wives, all of whom have borne him children.

His third wife, perhaps his most beloved, has a single daughter—Lilian Alderford. She is a prodigy who rose to the peak of the Root Master stage at just 19. Many praise and adore her, but many also envy her.
Perhaps due to this, she has been bedridden for the past five months, and regardless of how hard the healers on the Alderford payroll tried, they never seemed to understand what was happening.
"Master Shadrach, do you know what is wrong with her?" a beautiful lady who seemed to be in her late 30s asked, tears rolling down her cheek.

This lady is Cynthia Alderford, the third wife of John Alderford and mother of Lilian Alderford. The man she asked was the best alchemist and healer they had in the family. But even he didn’t have an answer for what was happening to Lilian.
There were no signs, no symptoms, nothing strange to suggest a diagnosis. She had simply fallen asleep and never woken up. She looked peaceful as if resting, still alive but not fully here.

"I’m sorry, miss, but even my abilities have their limits," Master Shadrach said, standing to leave. He had no cure. Without a diagnosis, he couldn’t even begin to prepare one. There was nothing more he could do.
After he left, a woman in her late 20s, probably a servant, approached Cynthia, taking her trembling hands in her own. Cynthia’s tears had soaked her face.
"Unity, do you think she’ll ever wake up?" Cynthia whispered, her voice breaking. She called the woman Unity.
Unity stayed silent for a few seconds, then replied softly, "Let’s just give it a little more time. Her temperature has been rising these past few days. Maybe... maybe that’s a sign."
"What if it’s not?" Cynthia’s voice was desperate. "What if something terrible happens? I can’t lose her, Unity. She’s my only daughter," she sobbed, her tears flowing freely.
"She won’t die, my love." A deep voice suddenly filled the room as John Alderford entered. Unity stepped back as he approached his wife.

"I’ve sent people to search for healers and alchemists across the kingdom," he said gently. "Anyone who can help our daughter. I’ll offer a generous reward, even if it means giving her hand in marriage to the one who saves her. I just want her alive."

Cynthia looked at him, torn. "You can’t do that, John. You know the Ashland family won’t accept it. Lilian is supposed to marry their second son. I want her well, but we can’t make enemies with them."
John let out a sharp breath, showing how little he cared about the consequences.
"It’s too late now," he said firmly. "The best healers and alchemists are on their way. They’ll start arriving in two days."

He took her hand, his gaze intense. "When I sent word to the Ashland family about Lilian’s condition, they had no response. Not a word. So why should we care about their feelings? If it comes to it, I’ll go to war to give my daughter a full life."

Although he may not look it due to his slim physique, John Alderford is actually a powerful cultivator at the peak of the Root Saint stage. He’s quite skilled with the spear, so if it came to it, he wouldn’t hesitate to fight. After all, he has some of the finest cultivators under his payroll and control.
Cynthia wanted to say something, but seeing the firm look in John’s eyes, she held back, letting him vent his anger in his own way.

Back on Forest Hill Mountain, inside the makeshift apartment where Master James Hogan used to live. Kent, who had been practicing his Sword Mind technique for the past four days, suddenly snapped his eyes open. In his silver-purple gaze, a flash of golden energy appeared.
"I’ve made some progress, but not enough to finally step into the Adept Swordsman stage," Kent muttered, reading the message that appeared as he opened his eyes.
[Congratulations, Master. Your understanding of the sword grows stronger. Current Progress: 65%.]

He had gained just 20% progress more after four full days of practice. The Sword Mind technique required him to train his mind to connect with the sword’s intent, achieved through constant visions of sword battles he experienced while practicing.
It was a strange way to learn the sword, but somehow, Kent loved it.
Now, he has moved past the visions of sword battles, which were actually sword intent being projected into visions, so he could watch while practicing the sword firsthand in his mind.
As his mind enters the sword, his consciousness begins to practice based on the hidden teachings embedded in the technique he is studying.
Kent doesn’t fully understand how, but somehow, he sees sword moves in his mind, which he only has to replicate.
Complex? Yes.
Weird? Definitely.
But is it effective? 100%. Although he hasn’t held the sword yet, he can tell his mastery is already very high, and he would be able to use it more effectively regardless of how he’s practicing.

He even asked the Tower how it was possible for him to see those visions and sword moves, but all it said was that everything is linked to the Sword Tower and his Legacy, and that he would learn more about it in the future when he unlocks the Tower.
"Huh, I have some visitors," Kent suddenly said, standing up. Five kilometers away, five soldiers riding in a carriage were headed toward his small home.
His master had left it for him, after all.

"Huh, Tower, how was I able to see that far even though I wasn’t looking at them directly?" Kent asked, puzzled. Just now, he had sensed a disturbance, and strangely, he could see them as if he were facing them.

"[It’s called Divine Sense, which you awakened when you broke through to the Root Blossom Stage. However, because of your strong mind and soul, you can see ten times farther than the average Root Blossom Stage expert.]"

"Awesome," Kent smiled, using his senses to keep track of the soldiers as they approached his home. He could tell their cultivation base, though the Tower had already informed him he didn’t need to, as it could help him with that.
Nonetheless, he wanted to test if he had the ability to perceive the depths of others’ cultivation bases.
A few minutes later, they arrived and knocked on the door.
"Master James Hogan, you have been summoned."

chapters.title: Chapter 18: Heading to Caprath City
paragraphs: Kent walked to the door and opened it with a smile on his face.
"Gentlemen, welcome to my home," he said, extending his hand for a firm handshake. The soldier looked him up and down, not even bothering to accept the handshake.
"Who are you?" he asked. Of course, Kent wasn’t offended he refused his handshake.

"I am Kent, the one and only disciple of the late Master James Hogan," Kent replied, not even bothering to hide the fact that James had passed away unjustly. He could have simply said his master wasn’t around.
But then again, his grave was just a few minutes away, so lying wasn’t an option either.
"Then sorry for wasting your time. Have a nice day," the soldier said, turning to leave.
"May I at least know why you sought my master?" Kent asked. He already knew, as his master had known why they were there. He had his memories, after all.
"The head of the Alderford Merchant family needed his services, but since he is no more, there’s no need to trouble you anymore," the soldier said.
"Oh, I wouldn’t mind filling in for my master. After all, he taught me everything he knew, so it would only be logical if I filled in for him," Kent said.
The soldier hesitated, looking Kent over. He seemed unsure for a moment but then nodded.
"Well, if you are willing, we can take you to the Alderford family. The head is in need of assistance with an urgent matter."
Their master had said they shouldn’t return empty-handed, so they wouldn’t be returning empty-handed.

"Then give me a few minutes to get my affairs in order so we can leave," Kent said before moving back inside. He stood in front of the cauldron and gently placed it inside the space ring. He moved toward the other room and retrieved a sword his master had hidden under his wooden bed.
It was slightly better than the one he was using to train. Of course, it was. After all, James Hogan had bought it for 70 gold coins. It was one of his most valuable possessions.
After collecting all the valuables he might need, Kent left the house and headed toward the carriage where the five soldiers were waiting for him.
"We can leave now," Kent said, climbing into the carriage.
The soldiers nodded and began moving back toward Caprath City.
Kent wasn’t particularly comfortable in the carriage, so halfway through their trip, he got out and began riding in the open area of the carriage. He wanted to see more of the outside.

"So, what is the Alderford Merchant family like?" Kent suddenly asked. "Don’t get me wrong, I just wanted to know so I can make a good impression. I haven’t been around such influential people before—until today, that is."
The soldiers hesitated for a minute before one of them spoke up. "Well, there are 13 merchant families in Caprath City, and the Alderford is within the top 5. They are highly influential."
"I see. I guess I’ll have to try my best to honor my master’s legacy," Kent said. The soldiers exchanged glances, as if they wanted to ask something, but hesitated.
Kent read their expressions and immediately knew what they wanted to ask.

"Don’t worry. Although I was trained by Master James, I’m not that shameless," Kent smiled. "Well, maybe a little shameless, but I promise I won’t be a nuisance to the Alderford family," he added, making the soldiers smile slightly.
"By the way, I presume my master wasn’t the only one summoned?" Kent asked.
"Yes, others have gone to the other cities to see if they can get some other alchemist to come," one of the soldiers answered.
"Hmm... More, huh? This makes me wonder what they need this many alchemists for," Kent muttered, making sure the soldiers heard what he said.
After making sure he had their attention, Kent turned to them and asked, "You gentlemen wouldn’t happen to know why they need this many alchemists, would you?"
The soldiers didn’t say anything, which made Kent smile slightly. He added, "Come on, guys, telling me something small wouldn’t do any harm, would it?"
He studied their expressions and could tell they knew what was happening—they just didn’t want to say anything. Suddenly, one of them, named Steve, spoke up.

"One of the daughters of John Alderford is sick, but no healer has been able to diagnose her, so they were hoping a fresh perspective would go a long way." The soldiers tried to rebuke Steve, but seeing the thoughtful look that appeared on Kent’s face, they held back.
After a few moments, Kent spoke. "Thanks for telling me. And even though I can’t promise I’ll be able to cure her, I will certainly do my best."
"And hey, if by some miracle I manage to cure her, I’ll be sure to share the reward with you guys," Kent added, making the soldiers smile.
Kent thought for a moment, then asked, "Do you know what kind of symptoms she has? Or what kind of illness it might be?"
The soldiers exchanged looks, but none of them answered.
"Come on, you must have heard something about it," Kent pressed. "I can’t help without some idea of what I’m dealing with."
One of the soldiers shook his head. "We don’t know much. We were only told she’s very ill, but no one could figure out what’s wrong with her."
Kent frowned, then nodded. "I see. I guess I’ll have to figure it out on my own then."
He thought for a moment. "Has anyone tried using alchemical remedies on her yet?"
"No, not that we know of," another soldier replied. "They only sent for alchemists after the healers failed."
Kent nodded again, deep in thought. "Alright. I’ll do my best to help. But one last thing—how long has she been sick?"
"It’s been a couple of months now," Steve answered. "They’ve been looking for a solution since she first got sick."

"By the way, I wanted to ask, who are the rulers of this city?" Even his master didn’t know, as he rarely engaged in the affairs of the city.
"The Ashland Noble Family," Steve answered.
A while later, they entered the city, which was easy and simple considering they were from the Alderford Merchant Family. Their uniforms were enough to show they needed no introduction.
After an hour and a half of moving through the city and an empty road, they arrived in front of a huge mansion, or more like a collection of large houses that made up a mansion.
"This place is beautiful," Kent muttered, looking at the polished walls, tall buildings, and, well, the whole place exuded luxury.
"Looks like we are the last ones to arrive," Steve said, noting the dozens of carriages already parked. Kent got down, and then they began moving into the house.

A few minutes later, they were at the entrance of a large building, where dozens of individuals could be seen sitting. Some were talking among themselves, while others were minding their own business.

One didn’t need an introduction to know these people were alchemists. After all, they all had that arrogant aura that screamed they were better than everyone else. You could even see it on their faces.
The moment Kent walked in, the whole place quieted down. He scanned their arrogant faces, then shook his head and went to sit down.
However, just as he was about to sit down, an arrogant voice spoke, "Who is this brat, and what business does he have in the gathering of alchemists?"

chapters.title: Chapter 19: Young and Arrogant
paragraphs: Kent didn’t mind the arrogant remark. He just sat down, poured himself a cup of tea from the teapot on his table, and began sipping, looking rather chill considering the fact that some people were fuming all around.
Naturally, he wasn’t like that, but after spending a whole year with the Goddess of Hatred and Resentment, he had taken on that arrogant aura and developed a rather arrogant personality.
Under normal circumstances, he would have at least responded to the man and glanced at him, but Kent didn’t even bother to give him that satisfaction. This made the man’s blood boil.

Suddenly, Kent felt an aura locking onto him. From the pressure, he sensed the person was a Peak Root Master—two realms above him. But just as the weight of the aura began to bear down on him, it vanished.
Kent snorted, turning toward the person who had just tried to intimidate him with their aura.
The shocked look on the man’s face spoke volumes. He hadn’t expected his Root Master aura to have so little effect.
"You should respect yourself, old man," Kent said calmly, his tone gentle, yet his words cutting. "Not everyone takes kindly to having some filthy aura try to probe them."
The face of the old man turns green hearing him call his aura filthy. That was a huge disrespect.
"By the way, I am the one and only disciple of the late Master James Hogan," Kent added.
"Wait, you’re a disciple of that shameful alchemist who lived in the mountains?" Another figure spoke up. It was Master Yuan, a somewhat respected alchemist, but his words didn’t sit well with Kent.
"It would be wise to address my late master with all due respect," Kent said, his gaze cold as he glanced sideways at Master Yuan. "Just because he had his shortcomings doesn’t mean he was shameful."
"Tsk..." Master Yuan clicked his tongue.
"I think we all know that good-for-nothing got what was coming to him. I only hope he died screaming." The alchemist who had tried to intimidate Kent earlier said, his face twisted with disdain.

"The good thing is he is dead, and it seems his legacy is rather arrogant. Clearly, the apple doesn’t fall far from the tree," another alchemist named Master Dan said wearing a disdainful expression on his face.

Almost all of them had that expression, clearly, they all hated the late James Hogan. Kent, who had his memories, knew hate was just them being generous. The bastard, the late master of his, was an unruly one.
He had scammed every one of them to the point where, instead of staying in the city, he ran off to the mountains and remained there for a couple of years.
Kent wanted to defend him, but doing so would infuriate them to the point where they wouldn’t mind killing him. After all, his master’s legacy was living on in him now.

"I can see you all hated my master, which is normal considering he was better than all of you. That being said, I plan on paying his debt, so after I help the Alderford family, I will come look for you all and pay back what he owed you," Kent boldly stated.

"Hahahah... Indeed, the apple doesn’t fall far from the tree. To think a disciple of a no-good-name alchemist thinks he has a chance at helping a whole merchant family... I wonder where this confidence of yours is coming from."
Kent smirked, his eyes narrowing as he spoke again. "You think I’m just like him, don’t you? Maybe you’re right. Maybe I am just as arrogant. But at least I have the power to back it up."
"Unlike him, I don’t run away. I’ll face all of you, and I’ll win. You’re all too weak to stop me."
Kent paused, then continued a few seconds later, "So keep laughing. It won’t matter when I’m standing on top, and you’re all forgotten."
At this, the faces of all fifteen alchemists gathered contorted with anger, ready to explode. Kent, however, just kept a smug smile as he calmly sipped his tea.
The Tower had already given him their data. From what he knew, the best among them was Master Yuan, who could concoct an 80% pure Tier 1 pill. The rest were somewhere between 45% and 75%.

According to the Tower, none of them had the strength to take him on in a fight—unless, of course, they chose a different type of battle. But even if it came down to concocting a Tier 0 pill, he would still wipe the floor with them.
After all, his purity level was about 90%, something none of them could boast.

"Everyone, welcome to my Alderford Family." Just when their anger was about to burst open, John Alderford entered the room, immediately drawing everyone’s attention. The spotlight shifted from Kent to him.
"I know you’ve all traveled from far and wide, so I won’t waste your time. The reason I summoned you here is because of my daughter, Lilian.

"Some of you may know of her—she’s one of the rising stars in this kingdom, having already become an Inner Disciple at the Divine Palace Sect and possessing a Platinum grade spirit root. However, five months ago, while visiting, she fell asleep and never woke up.
"We’ve had the best healers examine her, but none could diagnose the problem. We’ve tried everything, but nothing has worked.
"So, I’ve called you all here in the hope that one of you can help. And if you do, rest assured, you will be generously rewarded."
The alchemists looked at each other as if trying to wonder many things. In the end, Master Yuan decided to speak for them.
"Fear not, Lord Alderford. We are some of the best rogue alchemists out there. We will do our best to see that your beloved daughter is cured."
"Thank you, Master Yuan." John Alderford was about to add something, but before he could, Master Yuan continued.
"Lord Alderford, if it’s not too much to ask, could you please tell us exactly how long it’s been since she fell asleep?"

"Five months as of last week," he replied. The alchemists frowned, their expressions shifting. They’d been considering common illnesses, but after hearing this, they all set that idea aside, deep in thought again.
"Tsk." Suddenly, Kent chuckled, drawing everyone’s attention. "You guys won’t be able to cure her. The looks on your faces say it all."
"And you would be able to?" Master Dan asked, clearly angered by Kent’s remark.
"Of course. I’m not an idiot like you bunch, who immediately assumed she had sleep paralysis," Kent replied, his words making their expressions darken.

"That being said, I won’t steal the spotlight. I’ll let you fools pretend to diagnose her. After all, even if she were to sleep for ten years, nothing would happen. In fact, the poison running through her system won’t kill her for another hundred years—if her lifespan lasts that long," Kent said calmly.
"What?" John Alderford shouted. "What did you just say?" He moved toward Kent, who, despite John’s imposing presence, sat calmly with his teacup in hand.
"No need for the dramatics, Lord Alderford."
Kent took a slow sip of his tea, savoring the moment before finally continuing.

"Your daughter has been poisoned with Black Serpent’s Dream—a rare toxin designed to keep its victim in a deep, dreamless sleep. It’s subtle and potent, crafted to go undetected by typical diagnostic methods. Only an alchemist with skill and knowledge beyond the average could have done this."
The room fell silent.
Kent smiled in his head and said inwardly, ’Who needed a close-up diagnosis when they have a Tower’
