chapters.title: Chapter 20: Getting Hired
paragraphs: The room fell silent, every alchemist’s face now a mix of shock and frustration. John Alderford’s expression darkened as he looked into Kent’s eyes.
"Are you certain?" he demanded, his voice laced with both desperation and anger.
Kent met his gaze, unfazed.

"Absolutely. And let me be clear, Lord Alderford: none of these so-called experts would have ever figured it out. Black Serpent’s Dream is exceedingly rare, nearly forgotten. I’d wager a thousand gold coins that none of them have ever heard of before today."
He glanced around the room, letting his words sink in. He was clearly enjoying the moment.

"So, you can let them try all their outdated methods, or you can let me handle this. I’m the only one here with the knowledge and skill to create the antidote. But if you want your daughter cured, you’ll have to trust me completely."
The alchemists bristled with anger, but none dared challenge him. Kent’s words held a confidence that left them uneasy—and John Alderford had to decide quickly.
John Alderford stared at Kent, his expression a mixture of hope and caution.
"You’re saying you can cure her?" John asked, his voice barely above a whisper.
Kent nodded. "Yes. I can make the antidote. But it’s not simple. Black Serpent’s Dream requires a special remedy, one that must be prepared carefully and administered over several days."
The other alchemists exchanged uneasy glances. They hated admitting it, but Kent’s confidence was unshakable, and none of them had a solution of their own.
John took a deep breath, steadying himself. "Fine. I’ll trust you," he said, his voice firm. "Whatever resources you need, they’re yours. Just bring my daughter back."
At this point, Master Yuan and co knew they had lost to Kent who looked even more smug at the moment. The only thing they can hope for is for Kent to fail so they can win back their dignity somehow.
Kent smirked, setting his teacup down with a soft clink. "Good choice, Lord Alderford. I’ll need rare ingredients—items that aren’t easy to find. Some are even dangerous to obtain."
John nodded quickly. "Tell me what you need. I’ll make sure you have it."

Kent rose from his seat, his voice low but clear. "Then prepare yourself. This cure won’t be cheap, and it won’t be easy. But if you follow my lead, your daughter will wake up within the next seven days."
John Alderford nodded.
"Then take me to her so I can examine her current state," Kent said. He moved forward, following John. However, before walking out of the room, he turned to face the fifteen alchemists.
"Remember this failure and know it was caused by the one and only disciple of Master James Hogan."

With those words, Kent left with John Alderford, leaving behind a room full of angry alchemists. They could only grit their teeth and seethe in their anger, hoping he would fail to cure her in seven days as he had promised.
Deep down, though, they knew the chances of that happening were next to none. His confidence spoke volumes.
A few minutes later, Kent and John Alderford entered a new building where Cynthia Alderford and Unity were tending to Lilian Alderford’s beautiful, sleeping form.
"Who is this?" Cynthia immediately asked the moment her eyes settled on Kent.
"He’s the young man who thinks he can cure our daughter," John said, making no attempt to show confidence in Kent.
Kent, however, smiled and said, "I am Kent, and I’ve come to examine your daughter if you don’t mind."
Cynthia Alderford didn’t respond immediately and simply gestured for Unity to step aside so Kent could get a full view of Lilian’s current state.

Unity gave him a curious look, but Kent paid no mind to it. He walked closer, and because of the thin gown she was wearing, he was able to observe more than just her face. But he didn’t grow lustful, as one might think.
"As expected, like a sleeping beauty, she slept," Kent muttered. A few seconds later, he turned to face three curious pairs of eyes.

He smiled and said, "Relax, everyone. She is not in any danger." He stepped away from the bedside. "In fact, she might even be able to hear everything you all have said since the moment she fell asleep." The three exchanged looks.
"So, can you cure her?" John Alderford asked.
"But of course. Now, if you can give me something to write on, I’ll provide the list of ingredients needed to prepare the antidote for her."
Unity rushed out and returned a minute later, holding a scroll and a writing stick. Kent admired the items briefly, then began writing the ingredients.
He only needed six of the twenty-five ingredients he’d listed for the antidote. However, since he needed the extras for his own purposes, he decided to play it smart and earn something upfront.

"You can have your people collect these ingredients as soon as possible," Kent said, handing the list to John Alderford. He then added, "Personally, I recommend a group of five soldiers with a leader named Steve. He’s a good one."
John nodded and handed the list to Unity. "Find those five and have them collect these ingredients within the hour."

Unity nodded and left with the list. Kent looked toward the sleeping Lilian and asked, "I know it’s none of my business, but who would want to poison her? The poison used is rather rare, so while they didn’t want to kill her, they certainly went through a lot of trouble just to put her to sleep."
The husband and wife exchanged glances, but it was clear they had no idea why something like this had happened.

Lilian is a genius, admired by many. She quickly rose through the ranks, attaining the Peak Root Master stage when she was just 19, and she even became an Inner Sect Disciple at the Divine Palace Sect, one of the best sects in the Althea Kingdom.

One might wonder why someone like her would be poisoned to sleep rather than killed outright. The answer, however, is quite simple: they didn’t kill her because they couldn’t—or, more precisely, they failed to kill her.
The reason is straightforward: it’s because of her constitution. According to the data gathered by the tower, this was what was known about Lilian.
Name: Lilian Alderford
Age: 19
Bloodline: Dormant (Unawakened)
Constitution: Nine Life Divine body
Class: Mage
Cultivation: Root Master - Lvl 9/9
Physical Strength: 695
Spiritual Strenght: 1075
Mental Strength: 940

The Tower explained her constitution as one that allowed her to live nine times. This meant that even if she died, her cells alone would enable her to revive and continue living. It was a rare physique, and, well, perhaps some people had discovered it.

However, the Tower again made him know perhaps, that some people were after her Spirit Root and that if they managed to obtain it, they would be able to obtain both her talent and her Nine Life Divine body constitution.

Killing her with a lethal poison would have destroyed her Spirit Root, rendering whatever sinister plan they had useless. So, they used the Black Serpent’s Dream to put her to sleep while they prepared their next move.
Unfortunately for them, Kent had arrived like a knight in shining armor to cure her.
"That being said, I’ll do my best to cure her. Beauties aren’t supposed to sleep; they’re meant to shine as they walk about," Kent said with a smile.
A few hours later, the last of the ingredients were brought in.

sentences.text: The room fell silent, every alchemist’s face now a mix of shock and frustration.
John Alderford’s expression darkened as he looked into Kent’s eyes.
"Are you certain?" he demanded, his voice laced with both desperation and anger.
Kent met his gaze, unfazed.
"Absolutely.
And let me be clear, Lord Alderford: none of these so-called experts would have ever figured it out.
Black Serpent’s Dream is exceedingly rare, nearly forgotten.
I’d wager a thousand gold coins that none of them have ever heard of before today."
He glanced around the room, letting his words sink in.
He was clearly enjoying the moment.
"So, you can let them try all their outdated methods, or you can let me handle this.
I’m the only one here with the knowledge and skill to create the antidote.
But if you want your daughter cured, you’ll have to trust me completely."
The alchemists bristled with anger, but none dared challenge him.
Kent’s words held a confidence that left them uneasy—and John Alderford had to decide quickly.
John Alderford stared at Kent, his expression a mixture of hope and caution.
"You’re saying you can cure her?" John asked, his voice barely above a whisper.
Kent nodded.
"Yes.
I can make the antidote.
But it’s not simple.
Black Serpent’s Dream requires a special remedy, one that must be prepared carefully and administered over several days."
The other alchemists exchanged uneasy glances.
They hated admitting it, but Kent’s confidence was unshakable, and none of them had a solution of their own.
John took a deep breath, steadying himself.
"Fine.
I’ll trust you," he said, his voice firm.
"Whatever resources you need, they’re yours.
Just bring my daughter back."
At this point, Master Yuan and co knew they had lost to Kent who looked even more smug at the moment.
The only thing they can hope for is for Kent to fail so they can win back their dignity somehow.
Kent smirked, setting his teacup down with a soft clink.
"Good choice, Lord Alderford.
I’ll need rare ingredients—items that aren’t easy to find.
Some are even dangerous to obtain."
John nodded quickly.
"Tell me what you need.
I’ll make sure you have it."
Kent rose from his seat, his voice low but clear.
"Then prepare yourself.
This cure won’t be cheap, and it won’t be easy.
But if you follow my lead, your daughter will wake up within the next seven days."
John Alderford nodded.
"Then take me to her so I can examine her current state," Kent said.
He moved forward, following John.
However, before walking out of the room, he turned to face the fifteen alchemists.
"Remember this failure and know it was caused by the one and only disciple of Master James Hogan."
With those words, Kent left with John Alderford, leaving behind a room full of angry alchemists.
They could only grit their teeth and seethe in their anger, hoping he would fail to cure her in seven days as he had promised.
Deep down, though, they knew the chances of that happening were next to none.
His confidence spoke volumes.
A few minutes later, Kent and John Alderford entered a new building where Cynthia Alderford and Unity were tending to Lilian Alderford’s beautiful, sleeping form.
"Who is this?" Cynthia immediately asked the moment her eyes settled on Kent.
"He’s the young man who thinks he can cure our daughter," John said, making no attempt to show confidence in Kent.
Kent, however, smiled and said, "I am Kent, and I’ve come to examine your daughter if you don’t mind."
Cynthia Alderford didn’t respond immediately and simply gestured for Unity to step aside so Kent could get a full view of Lilian’s current state.
Unity gave him a curious look, but Kent paid no mind to it.
He walked closer, and because of the thin gown she was wearing, he was able to observe more than just her face.
But he didn’t grow lustful, as one might think.
"As expected, like a sleeping beauty, she slept," Kent muttered.
A few seconds later, he turned to face three curious pairs of eyes.
He smiled and said, "Relax, everyone.
She is not in any danger." He stepped away from the bedside.
"In fact, she might even be able to hear everything you all have said since the moment she fell asleep." The three exchanged looks.
"So, can you cure her?" John Alderford asked.
"But of course.
Now, if you can give me something to write on, I’ll provide the list of ingredients needed to prepare the antidote for her."
Unity rushed out and returned a minute later, holding a scroll and a writing stick.
Kent admired the items briefly, then began writing the ingredients.
He only needed six of the twenty-five ingredients he’d listed for the antidote.
However, since he needed the extras for his own purposes, he decided to play it smart and earn something upfront.
"You can have your people collect these ingredients as soon as possible," Kent said, handing the list to John Alderford.
He then added, "Personally, I recommend a group of five soldiers with a leader named Steve.
He’s a good one."
John nodded and handed the list to Unity.
"Find those five and have them collect these ingredients within the hour."
Unity nodded and left with the list.
Kent looked toward the sleeping Lilian and asked, "I know it’s none of my business, but who would want to poison her?
The poison used is rather rare, so while they didn’t want to kill her, they certainly went through a lot of trouble just to put her to sleep."
The husband and wife exchanged glances, but it was clear they had no idea why something like this had happened.
Lilian is a genius, admired by many.

She quickly rose through the ranks, attaining the Peak Root Master stage when she was just 19, and she even became an Inner Sect Disciple at the Divine Palace Sect, one of the best sects in the Althea Kingdom.
One might wonder why someone like her would be poisoned to sleep rather than killed outright.
The answer, however, is quite simple: they didn’t kill her because they couldn’t—or, more precisely, they failed to kill her.
The reason is straightforward: it’s because of her constitution.
According to the data gathered by the tower, this was what was known about Lilian.

Bloodline: Dormant (Unawakened)
Constitution: Nine Life Divine body
Class: Mage

chapters.title: Chapter 21: Preparing the Antidote
paragraphs: Because of the hard work of the guards, the ingredients were gathered faster than anyone could have expected. Kent was rather pleased with how quickly the guards managed to collect the ingredients. He made a mental note to contact them in the future to help him gather herbs.

After obtaining the ingredients, he requested a secluded place where he could work. The pill he was about to make was only a Tier 0 pill, but even with just six ingredients, he needed to prepare carefully. This was also why he had asked for more than he needed.
He wanted to practice more and, if possible, push his purity level a little higher to craft a better pill next time.
Unity led him to a room not far from the main building and stood guard outside, ensuring that no one disturbed him while he worked.
Once he was gone, John Alderford and his wife began a conversation.
"Do you think he can cure her?" Cynthia asked.

"So far, so good. He’s been the only one able to come up with a diagnosis. Whether he can cure her depends on his capabilities. But I guess we’ll find out in a few days," John said, still wearing a skeptical expression.
It would take more than a diagnosis to earn their trust. But Kent knew this, and he planned to build his reputation as an alchemy genius from here.
"So, about your promise—are you willing to give her hand to him if he does manage to cure her?" Cynthia asked.

"I didn’t say anything to either of them when I spoke with the alchemist earlier on... I never got the chance. But if he does manage to cure her, I wouldn’t mind giving her to him. Someone this young and brilliant is destined to become someone great in the future."
Cynthia sighed. "He is indeed capable. Let’s just give him a few days to see if he can help her. If the end is destined to happen, we can only prepare for the repercussions."
The two continued their conversation. Meanwhile, in the room assigned to Kent, he laid out the ingredients and began heating the cauldron. He first wanted to practice before the real deal
When it was hot enough, he added the first ingredient, followed by the next after extracting its essence. The others followed in sequence, one by one until all were in the cauldron.
"If only I could just put them all in and extract the essence at the same time... wouldn’t that be much more convenient," Kent muttered.
[The master can practice complete extraction, but that would require precise flame control that the master currently lacks,] the tower commented bluntly.
"You could have said it more nicely, tower," Kent chuckled.
[The master could try mastering the Seven Flame Control and Refining Art; it would open more doors for him,] the tower suggested, and Kent smiled.

"I tried, but I can tell that technique requires a significant amount of spiritual energy, which I currently lack due to my low cultivation base. Besides, I don’t have ingredients to waste right now," Kent said, shaking his head.

Inside his dantian, a large amount of yin qi, rich with divinity, was stored. However, without a Spirit Core in his dantian, he couldn’t use it yet; he would need to cultivate manually or dual cultivate to progress.
[Because the master has now inherited the Sword Tower, he can start cultivating again to level up,] the tower reminded him.
"I know, tower, but let me finish this first before we think about that."
After several minutes, dark smoke drifted from the cauldron, escaping through the windows. It was a sign that the pill was finished. Kent retrieved it and smiled.
[You have successfully concocted a Qi Gathering Pill. Grade: Tier 0, Quality: Excellent. Purity: 95%.]
"Looks like my progress is improving, even after a few days without touching the cauldron," he said before tossing the pill into his space ring.
[You are making great progress, Master,] the tower remarked.
"That I am, Tower," Kent replied, then took out the real ingredients for the antidote. He examined them for a few minutes before standing up and stepping outside the room.
When he emerged, Unity was there, looking curious and slightly flustered for obvious reasons. The reason, of course, was Kent, who walked out bare-chested.
Being from Earth, the concept of men covering their bodies all day wasn’t something he could easily adapt to.

Although the temperature inside the room hadn’t been that hot, Kent wanted to feel the air on his skin for the next few hours as he worked. After all, he had spent a whole year naked in the god realm; old habits die hard.
"Do you need something, Master Kent?" Unity asked, trying her best not to glance at his finely toned six-pack and muscular arms.
"You can skip the formalities and just call me Kent," he said with a small smile. "And please, could you get me a glass of water?"
"Right away," Unity replied, quickly running off.
[She’s not bad, Master. She has a powerful bloodline that hasn’t awakened yet, along with an unwakened unique constitution,] the tower noted.
"I know, Tower. She’s not bad at all, just a little uptight," Kent replied as if talking to the tower was the most natural thing in the world.

"That being said, she’s indeed not bad," Kent mused before stepping back inside. A few minutes later, Unity returned with the water, then quickly left the room, clearly not wanting to spend another moment staring at Kent’s physique.
He could only smile before starting his next pill. Once the cauldron was hot enough, he added the first ingredient and began extracting its essence.
Twenty minutes later, he added the last ingredient to the cauldron. Though he wanted to finish quickly to move on to other tasks, he still took his time to increase the purity level.
An hour and twenty minutes later, the pill was complete, and a message appeared, bringing a smile to his lips.
[You have successfully concocted a Black Serpent’s Dream Antidote Pill. Grade: Tier 0, Quality: Excellent. Purity: 97%.]
"I am a natural," Kent smiled.
[That you are, Master,] the tower, ever the hype man, didn’t fail to drop a comment.

Kent poured small drops of water into the cauldron and used the flame to burn it, ensuring it was clean. Although the pill was an antidote, it still contained traces of poison, and since he didn’t want his purity level to be affected, he first used a method to clean it before tackling the next pill.
Twelve hours later, seven pill boxes lay before him, with the highest purity being 98%. It was the last pill he concocted after resting for a few hours.
He got dressed, put away the boxes containing the pills, and left the room.
"Are you already done?" Unity was shocked when she saw him outside.
"Yup. It was just a Tier 0 pill, no need to spend days on it," Kent casually replied, making sure to add a few extra words.
"I see," Unity said calmly.
"Then we can go now," Kent said, gesturing forward. Soon, they were back in the room where Lilian was sleeping.
"Are you done already?" John Alderford asked, clearly taken aback.
"I work fast, Lord Alderford. I work fast," Kent said with a small smile before walking toward Lilian.

chapters.title: Chapter 22: Curing Lilian
paragraphs: "Now, while I would love to have all of you here, it would be best if you excuse me for the next few days. And don’t worry, I won’t let anything happen to her," Kent said after walking to the side of Lilian’s bed.
John and Cynthia Alderford looked at each other and then nodded. They, along with Unity, began to move out, but Kent’s voice stopped Unity.
"I will be needing an assistant." Unity knew she was the one he was asking for; the husband-and-wife duo also knew, so without even bothering to ask her, Unity stepped back, walking toward the bed.
John and Cynthia left.
"How can I be of help?" Unity asked.
"Help me raise her head slightly," Kent said. Unity nodded and did as she was told.

Kent retrieved the first of the seven pills and dissolved it in water before bringing it closer to Lilian’s mouth. Although she looked peaceful and beautiful, she was deep asleep, thanks to the poison sending her into a dreamless state for God knows how long.
He used his hand to force open her jaw and then gently poured in the antidote, now in liquid form. After administering the antidote, Unity places her back on the bed.
"She will wake up in a few hours, but don’t call anyone. Just come call me when she wakes up," Kent said before walking away, leaving Unity in a shocked state.
He did say it would take 7 days, so why was she suddenly waking up now, just a few hours after the first treatment was administered? The answer was simple—Kent wanted some alone time with her.
That being said, he went back to the room where he concocted the pill and began practicing the sword in his mind, making sure to use every last second to learn something.
Eighteen hours later, inside the room where Lilian was, a sudden cough came from the bed, making Unity, who was sitting a few meters away, quickly rush to the bed.
"Young miss, you are awake," she said, tears almost falling from her eyes as she held her hand.
"What happened, Unity?" Lilian asked in a tired voice.

"You were poisoned with a poison that put you into a sleep-like state for the past five months," Unity replied, making Lilian burst out shouting, but alas, she was too weak to entertain such dramatics.
"So it was true, huh?" she muttered. Although she was asleep, she managed to hear a few things.
"Give me a few minutes; let me go and call Master Kent," Unity said, standing up.
"Who is that?" Lilian asked.
"He is the alchemist curing you," Unity replied before running off.
"An alchemist?" Lilian muttered. "What happened to the healers?" she wondered, but alas, she could only sigh and wait for this mysterious Master Kent.
Inside the room where Kent was training, the Tower suddenly messaged him, waking him up from his focused state.
"So she is awake, huh?" Kent said, watching in the direction where Unity was running. A few seconds later, he heard a knock on the door.
"Master Kent, the young miss is awake," Unity said immediately after knowing.
"Alright, let’s go." With that, he left the room and headed to where Lilian was. A few minutes later, they arrived in the large room.
"Glad to see you’re awake," Kent said, flashing a cute smile. This smile, of course, held many perverted thoughts.
"You must be Master Kent, I suppose?" Lilian asked.
"The one and only, but you can just call me Kent; the master title makes me appear rather old," Kent laughed, and Lilian blushed a little. But it wasn’t just her—Unity was the same.

Kent, however, didn’t mind their looks. His focus was rather on whether or not to use the next few days to seduce her or just outright use the Divine Pervert hand skill. He had decided on his next moves and Lilian and Unity would be part of those plans.
In the end, he remembered what Vexthra had told him and decided to use his words instead. He can’t force any lady and using his skill on them while they don’t consent wasn’t the way forward.

"You are still too weak to do anything, so I will be leaving these 6 pills with you. Take one each day and try not to walk out. Unity will stay with you, and after you are done with the last pill, tell her to come call me."
With that, Kent left, not even bothering to stay there for another minute.
"Well, that is a first," Unity said, walking toward Lilian.
"What do you mean?" Lilian asked.

"Haven’t you noticed? He doesn’t seem to be charmed by your beauty, something that married men couldn’t even do, considering you are a number one beauty many will drool over," Unity said with a small smile.
It doesn’t take a genius to know the two are more than just a master and servant. They are great friends.
"Now that you mentioned it, I suppose he is different," Lilian said. "He even managed to make you, the almighty queen of absolute focus blush," she added.
"If only you could see your face too," Unity didn’t object; instead, she made sure Lilian knew she wasn’t the only one who blushed.
"Do you know who he is and where he’s from?" Lilian asked.

"I don’t, but he seems capable, and from the look of things, very powerful, so I wouldn’t be shocked if he’s a disciple of one of those infamous Grandmaster Alchemists," Unity said, making Lilian nod.
If only they knew the person in question was a mere unofficial disciple of the late Master James Hogan, also known as the Shameless Alchemist. A rather hilarious backstory.
For the next 6 days, Lilian took the pills as she was instructed to. These past six days were also spent discussing only one topic, and that topic was the mysterious Kent.
On the fourth day, she was strong enough to begin moving, but she didn’t go out or call for his parents since Unity told her Kent wanted her to stay in until he was done with his last examination.

However, that didn’t prevent her from using her divine sense to spy on Kent, who, for the past 6 days, had been practicing the sword, pushing his mastery to the Adept stage while concocting Pills on the side.

Right after she and Unity spent a great deal of their spiritual qi every single day spying on him, they would then talk a great deal about him. After that, the next day, they would repeat the same thing.
When she was done with the last pill, Unity went to call Kent.

"Congratulations, the toxin is out of your system. You can use the next few days to rest if you want," Kent said after checking her temperature by placing his hand on her forehead. A gesture that made Lilian’s heartbeat rise by several degrees.
"Thank you, Master... thank you, Kent," Lilian said with a blush.
"It was the least I could do for a beauty such as yourself," Kent said before turning to Unity.
"You can go tell her parents she is awake and well. Two days from today, I would like you to escort me through the city since this is my first day here," Kent said before walking away.
"How mysterious," Lilian said, watching Kent walk away.
"Mysterious, but sexy," Unity added, turning her head sideways.
"I have made my decision. I will tell Father to let me be his woman," Lilian suddenly declared, making Unity smile faintly.
If only she knew that her father had already made such an arrangement.
Later, instead of calling her parents, she dressed up and went to meet them herself shocking them all.

chapters.title: Chapter 23: Going out
paragraphs: Somewhere in Caprath, inside a rather lavish room, a woman could be seen doing her makeup. Well, the sheer amount of makeup she wore was too much to simply be called makeup. She was practically remolding her face with paint.

This woman was Daisy Ashland, the second wife of Dave Ashland, the Lord of Caprath City. Daisy was one of the five wives Dave had married among his many concubines. She was both brilliant and, well, beautiful—makeup beautiful, at least.
Suddenly, in a certain corner of the room, a figure appeared.
"My Lady, we have a problem," the figure spoke.
"What is it?" Daisy asked, putting her makeup brush down.
"Lilian Alderford is awake," the figure said, shifting Daisy’s mood slightly. She was shocked to hear the report but quickly composed herself.
"How? How did it happen?" she asked in a stunned tone.

"A new alchemist by the name of Kent appeared on the scene a few days ago, and, to everyone’s shock, Lilian woke up perfectly fine. She’s even well enough to be taken back to the sect," the reporter said.
"What do we know of this new alchemist?" Daisy asked.
"He’s young and, well, he claims to be the disciple of that alchemist...the shameless alchemist."
"The one who ran and hid in the mountains?" Daisy asked.

"Yes. He’s just a Level 3 Root Blossom stage cultivator," the reporter added before asking, "My Lady, should I report this to Lord Dave? I made sure she would stay asleep until the Young Miss arrived, but it seems things might not go as planned."
"No," Daisy said. "I will do it myself. Just go back; I’ll handle the rest from here."

"As you say, my Lady," the figure bowed and left. A few minutes later, Daisy also left and went to another lavish building. The building was constructed with rare stones that seemed to absorb the spirit qi in the air.
Perhaps it was due to the formation placed around the room, but the spiritual qi there was unusually rich and plentiful.

In one of the rooms inside this enormous building, a man could be seen thrusting his body against a woman who seemed lost among the stars. He showed no mercy, and her moans filled the room, even echoing down the halls.
Daisy stopped in front of the door, and without knocking, she pushed it open and walked in.
"For heaven’s sake, Daisy, it’s not yet your turn, so why are you interrupting us?" the woman, bent at an unnatural angle, shouted.
"Shut up, Vida. We have a problem, so snap out of your horniness, and let’s talk about it," Daisy shouted back, and it seemed to work. Vida, the third wife of Dave Ashland, calmed down instantly.
"What is it, my love?" Dave asked, still moving his hips, but slower this time.

"Lilian Alderford has woken up because of some new alchemist," Daisy announced, causing Dave to thrust rather forcefully, making Vida yelp in pain. But Dave didn’t pay attention to her; he pulled away and moved toward Daisy.
"Are you sure?" he asked.
"Yes, I just got the report from our spy in the Alderford mansion," Daisy replied. "What should we do? We can’t let that spirit root slip through our fingers; we’ve invested a lot in this."

"We won’t. Our daughter will get that spirit root, no matter what," Dave said before turning to Vida. "Get that useless son of yours to go to the Alderford family and propose marriage to Lilian," he commanded.

"As you say, my Lord," Vida said, unhappy but obedient. In the Ashland family, they all knew that despite being only the second wife, Daisy was far more intelligent than the rest—even more than Dave himself—so they always deferred to her.
"And this new alchemist, what should we do about him?" Daisy asked.

"I’ll send some men to take him out the moment he steps out of the Alderford mansion," Dave replied. A few seconds later, Daisy was gone. Vida, although reluctant, also left to handle the task assigned to her.
"Damn it," Dave cursed. "Why so suddenly? I won’t let the only Platinum Grade Spirit Root in this city slip through my fingers," he added, clenching his fists. Soon, he, too, left the room.

The reason he was so intent on securing this spirit root for his daughter was that, in this world, Spirit Roots were everything. They determined one’s potential, and many believed that to ascend, one must possess a very high-grade spirit root.
Those known as prodigies typically had higher-grade spirit roots. In Lilian’s case, she had a Platinum Grade Spirit Root. This meant that someday she could potentially ascend to a higher realm.

In Sonox, there are eight different grades of spirit roots: Common, Copper, Silver, Gold, Diamond, Platinum, Ruby, and Dark Gold. The latter two are the rarest, but even Platinum is exceptionally rare.
So, when it was discovered that Lilian had a Platinum Grade Spirit Root, the Ashland family became envious and plotted to steal it for their daughter.

They had put Lilian to sleep and were waiting for the Alderford family to become desperate. Then they would swoop in, pretending to help her and take her away. The rest would depend on the specialist they had contracted to perform the transplant.
However, with Kent’s unexpected appearance, everything had changed. It now seemed likely that this grand opportunity would soon slip through their fingers.
Their next move has already been implemented.

But would they succeed? That question now rested on Kent, who had finally advanced to the Sword Adept stage. He was leaving the Alderford mansion with Unity to explore the city and possibly sell his Qi Gathering Pills.
But before leaving, he went to meet with John Alderford, who had requested an audience.
"Once again, thank you for helping my daughter, which was akin to helping my family," John Alderford said.
"I was just doing my job, Lord Alderford," Kent replied with a small smile.
"You can call me John, and please, take this token as a form of our appreciation," John said, handing over a pouch to Kent.

Kent reached out and received the pouch with a warm smile. The Tower had already counted the amount—it was 1000 spirit stones, equivalent to 100,000 gold coins. More than enough to secure the ingredients needed to improve his alchemy skills.
"Thank you, Lord... erm, John. But I have a request, I would like to request Unity to escort me around the city. It’s my first time here, and I want to get the full Caprath experience," Kent asked.
"Are you sure? Unity is just a level 4 Root Master. If you want, I can assign some Root Grandmaster guards to escort you," John proposed.
"I don’t need bodyguards, John; I just want a guide, and Unity is a rather pleasant guard," Kent said, casting a sidelong glance at Unity, who was standing beside Lilian and her mother.
"As you say, Master Kent," John said, turning to Unity. "You will accompany Master Kent. Make sure he feels welcomed in Caprath City," he instructed.
"Alright, my Lord," Unity bowed.
"Then I will see you all later." With that, Kent and Unity left, taking a rather fine-looking carriage to tour the city for the next few hours.
Back inside the hall, John and his family entered into a sudden discussion that seemed to revolve around Kent...

With four minutes left on his connection to Vexthra, he decided to engage the goddess in conversation.

chapters.title: Chapter 27: The Loophole In the Harem
paragraphs: Back in the God Realm, Vexthra, who had just made a cup of coffee and was about to drink it, felt a familiar connection form in her mind, bringing a small smile to her face. Then Kent’s voice entered her head.
<Hello there, my Sugar Goddess. How are you?> Kent greeted, making her smile widen.
"I am fine, Kent. How about you? Living your best life yet?" Vexthra asked.
<As a matter of fact, I am. Your soon-to-be sister is rather fond of my little dragon,> Kent transmitted, bringing a small blush to Vexthra’s face.
"I presume you aren’t contacting me to tell me you’re getting a blowjob," Vexthra asked.
<No. I just wanted to test a theory, that’s all.>
"Go ahead."

<You remember when you said giving me too much would cause the laws of the world to punish me? I think I’ve found a fix. Since I’m now in the Mortal World and have a system that allows me to contact you, technically, you can send me things... specifically, you can send me techniques for now,> Kent said.

"How would that be possible?" Vexthra asked. Truthfully, she wanted to give Kent all the best techniques she had and even the ones she could create out of thin air. But because of the laws restricting certain things, she wasn’t able to.
Now, it was different. Kent had a plan.
<I will be adding a second member to the harem, which means I can take two skills from her arsenal. This also means you can view her profile if I want you to, and you can even add something to it.
So, since you can’t add to mine, you can add whatever you have for me to hers, and then I will take it from her,> Kent explained, and Vexthra’s face lit up.
"Does this mean I can give you all the techniques you wanted? and who is my new Sister" she asked.

<Of course. Her name is Unity, a very lovely girl, and I know you’re going to love her. So why don’t you use the five minutes it’ll take to form the connection between you and her to get to know each other a little? Then, during that time, give me one technique—the sword one—and give her also a cultivation technique> Kent said.
"Okay, dear, this is great!" For some reason, Vexthra became rather happy.
<I know you’re the best,> Kent said, smiling as he gazed at Unity, who was about to have her destiny changed by joining a harem where her big sister was a goddess.
"Hurry up and link her. I want to meet my sister," Vexthra said, smiling.
<Okay... jeez, aren’t you the Goddess of Hatred and Resentment? Where is all this cheerfulness coming from?>
"From your d*ck, I think... It changed a lot of things for me," Vexthra admitted with a blush.
<Pervert,> Kent said before cutting the connection.

Vexthra smiled and returned to her coffee. Kent had made sure her home resembled that of someone from modern-day Earth. She had a toaster and everything. She was practically living the life of a mortal now.
Back in the carriage, Unity was giving Kent head, determined not to repeat the mistakes she made last time. After 15 minutes, Kent decided to let her have her way, releasing his load down her throat.
It took some gagging, but she endured it with a smile. After ensuring she had swallowed everything, Kent got serious and asked the question necessary to officially add someone to his harem.
"Unity, do you want to officially become my woman and join my harem?" he asked.
"Yes. I want to," Unity answered with a smile.
"Great," Kent said, smiling.
"Now, what I’m about to tell you will come as a shock but will also change your life. So listen carefully, and if you decide to renege on your answer, I wouldn’t hate you for it."
Unity suddenly became calm, focusing intently as she listened.
"First, there is someone already in the harem, so you would be the second member. However, this person is not a mortal like you and me... she is a goddess, and she lives in the God Realm."
"A goddess? Living in the God Realm?" Unity asked her tone a mix of awe and curiosity.
"Yes, and when I add you to the harem, she can talk to you for five minutes every 100 days. She’ll also give you a god-level technique that you can cultivate," Kent added.
"Are you serious?" Unity asked, her eyes wide with disbelief.
"Of course. Why would I lie to you?" Kent smiled. "So, now, do you want to join, or do you want to tap out?"
"I want to join even more now. I don’t know whether what you said is true or not, but I want to be your woman regardless," Unity said cheerfully.
"Good answer," Kent replied, then turned his attention to the Tower, his number one wingman at the moment.
<Add her to the Harem.>
The moment Kent gave the order, Unity felt a burning sensation just below her belly, causing her to flinch slightly.

When she looked down, she saw a tattoo of a tower appearing on her skin, intricate and glowing faintly. She stared at it in awe, her mind racing with questions. But before she could ask anything, however, a connection began forming in her mind.
"Have fun talking to your sister, Unity. She’s very lovely," Kent said with a knowing smile.
Moments later, a voice entered Unity’s head, causing her eyes to widen in shock and amazement.
Kent smiled to himself, satisfied that Vexthra had already made contact. Turning his attention away, he noticed a message had appeared before him, pulling his focus to what came next.
[Congratulations, Master. You have added the second woman to your harem: Unity Harper.]
[You have received a new skill that belongs to Unity. Skill Name: Teleport.]
<Teleport, huh? Tower, show me the details of the skill> Kent requested.
[Skill Name: Teleport]
[Grade: Earth Grade]
[Rank: A]
[Effect]
- As long as you have stamina, you can continuously teleport within ten-meter intervals. You must see where you want to teleport for the skill to work.
[Upgradable]
<A nice skill at least,> Kent smiled, knowing that although he could move faster than that, he could use this skill to surprise his enemies.
<Tower, how do I upgrade it?> Kent asked.
[You can use skill upgrade points that you earn through martial skills. Basically, you earn those from fighting and killing people/things] the tower explained, making Kent smile.
<All the more reason for me to join a sect where I’ll get to fight some fools,> Kent sighed. He then turned to his status page.
[Status] + [Harem] + [Alchemy] + [Bloodline Traits & Skills]
Name: Kent
Age: 18
Bloodline: Primordial Chaos Dragon
Class: Alchemist
Subclass: Swordsman
Cultivation: Root Blossom - Lvl 6/9
Physical Strength: 110
Physical Agility: 110
Physical Stamina: 140
Spiritual Strength: 300
Mental Strength: 210
[Tower Points: 60,000]
[Attribute Points: 200]
[Skill Upgrade Points: 0]
<Hmm, looks like I managed to earn 30 extra points from leveling up three times. I also have to distribute the 200 I have in store,> Kent pondered for a few moments before making up his mind.
<Tower, add 100 to stamina, 50 to strength, and the other 50 to agility.>
Immediately after giving the order, he felt his strength rise. His speed and endurance grew as well.
<That’s more like it,> he smiled, then went back to check some other things.
Four minutes later, Kent finished up and turned to Unity, who held a small smile on her face while talking with Vexthra.
A moment later, she smiled and said, "Thank you, Kent. You’ve made me the happiest woman in the entire universe."

chapters.title: Chapter 28: Who is Uncle Drew
paragraphs: Kent smiled at her statement, watching her sincere and passionate eyes. He knew at that moment that the woman in front of him would never even think of leaving him. Whatever Vexthra had told her, he could tell Unity had taken it to heart and would treasure it forever.
"I suppose you and Vexthra linked up quite well," Kent said, smiling.
"Indeed. Sister Vexthra is the best! She gave me a Divine-grade cultivation technique that is designed specifically for me and only me," Unity replied with a beaming smile.

Kent smiled again, knowing she had received more than she could have hoped for. Divine-grade techniques were rare beyond imagination. The grades of techniques and skills began at Mortal, Epic, Rare, Earth, Heaven, Legendary, Mystical, Primordial, Divine, Ancient, Supreme, and finally Celestial.
In this lower world, people would go to war for a mere Legendary technique. A Divine-grade technique was unheard of, it was a treasure beyond measure. Kent knew Unity’s future was secured forever.
"Congratulations on earning something so remarkable. I hope you use it well in the future—perhaps even become a goddess and meet her again someday," Kent said with a playful smile.

As for himself, the technique he requested from Vexthra was called Heaven Annihilation Strike. It, too, was a Divine-grade technique, but it was a martial technique designed to enhance his swordsmanship. The technique has seven forms, the first of which was called Rapid Slash.

This form allowed him to unleash quick and precise slashes infused with his sword aura. The stronger his sword aura, the deadlier his strikes would be. Moreover, the more he used the technique, the faster his sword aura would grow.

Kent had chosen this technique over many other incredible ones. However, Vexthra had initially refused to give him others, explaining that she had miscalculated the Tower’s effects after he inherited it. It has taken too much soul space for her to add more techniques without triggering the laws.
But now, Kent had discovered a loophole within the harem system. By adding more women to his harem, he could unlock and acquire all the skills and techniques he desired.
"Do you want to go one more round before we continue our journey?" Kent asked with a perverted smile, scanning Unity’s naked body.
"Uncle Drew is going to be pissed," Unity replied with a smile.
"Who is Uncle Drew?" Kent asked.
"The carriage driver," Unity replied, making Kent smile as well.

"I will reward him handsomely after this," Kent said as he reached for her hand. Before long, his full shaft entered her body, and he began thrusting in and out. After half an hour, Kent finished after Unity had climaxed three times.

They then dressed, with Unity taking a new outfit from her space ring since her first one was drenched. Kent, of course, wore the same clothes, as he had been quick to remove them before they could get soaked.

Soon, the carriage began moving again. Kent didn’t know the carriage driver, but from Unity’s expression, it seemed the two were rather close. This made him wonder what Uncle Drew might be feeling as Unity sang him praises.

After all, the fact that he had stopped the carriage to allow them their moment was enough to tell Kent that the old man was a man of culture. He decided he would reward him, even though he didn’t have much to give.
A few minutes later, they arrived in the city. Kent and Unity got down from the carriage.

"We’ll be gone for the next few hours. You can wait for us here," Kent said to Uncle Drew while Unity hid behind the carriage, clearly embarrassed by all the intimacy they had shared in the middle of the road.

"Take this, you’ve earned it," Kent said, handing 50 shining spirit stones to Uncle Drew. Each stone was equivalent to 100 gold coins, meaning the driver had just made 5,000 gold coins simply for riding two love-struck youths.
Uncle Drew received the spirit stones with a thankful gaze. Kent nodded in acknowledgment of his gratitude, and then he and Unity left.

Soon, they entered the bustling city, where a variety of faces could be seen going about their daily activities. Sellers were busy selling, and buyers eagerly buying. It was a cultivation world, after all, and countless goods were on offer.
Stores lined the streets, selling all manner of items, while some shopkeepers shamelessly shouted their advertisements to attract customers.
"Fresh spirit fruits! Guaranteed to boost your cultivation!" one vendor shouted, holding up a glowing basket of fruit.
"Top-grade talismans! Protection from demons and beasts! Only 10 gold coins each!" another seller yelled from a stall covered in shimmering charms.
"Rare herbs for alchemy! Limited stock! Don’t miss out!" a woman called, her table piled with bundles of vibrant plants.
"Weapons imbued with spirit energy! Strong and sharp, perfect for any battle!" a blacksmith bellowed, striking a glowing blade with his hammer.
"Storage rings. Affordable and spacious. Keep all your treasures safe." an elderly merchant announced, holding up glittering rings in various sizes.
The air buzzed with activity, each vendor trying to outshout the next.

"This place is more lively than I thought," Kent said with a happy expression. Because of his master’s shameless antics, he had always been running from one problem to the next, never really having good memories to relish.

Well, he did know a lot about brothels—his master had been into many of them. So, if Kent wanted to indulge, he knew exactly where to go. But alas, with Unity by his side and probably Lilian waiting for him later, such places were no longer an option. They felt outdated and unappealing.

"This city is known for its business. Many merchant families live here, so commerce in this place is taken very seriously," Unity said, walking beside the handsome Kent, who was already gathering admirers.

His handsomeness was striking, accentuated by his unique set of eyes and hair. After a year of intimacy with a goddess, her potent yin qi, though too strong for him to absorb, had somehow enhanced his looks. He now resembled a prince from some distant elf kingdom—too striking to go unnoticed.
"You seem to be attracting some looks," Unity said, her voice tinged with jealousy as she noticed the thirsty gazes following him.
"Don’t worry, my dear. They’re all look and no go," Kent replied with a charming smile. That smile only added fuel to the fire, causing some of the ladies in the crowd to openly drool.
"Now, let’s go to that alchemy store. I need some herbs—a lot of them," Kent said, pointing toward a shop filled with shelves of alchemy ingredients.
The first Pill Records contained only Tier 0 pill recipes, and Kent needed to concoct 120 of them, each with perfect purity. This, of course, meant he would need to buy a large number of ingredients.
If he wanted to make serious money, he would have to move up to concocting Tier 1 pills, which sold quite well in this kingdom.

There were also Tier 2, Tier 3, and even Tier 4 pills in existence, but Kent didn’t yet have the skills to make them. Even if he could, those pills were rare and expensive, both to craft and to purchase.
For now, he had to settle for Tier 0 pill ingredients, along with a small selection of Tier 1 ingredients to prepare for his future progress.
Once his mastery reached the level required to unlock the second Pill Records, he could begin concocting Tier 1 pills and, hopefully, progress to Tier 2 pills as well.
"What does this fine gentleman and lady wish to purchase this fine afternoon?" the store owner greeted them warmly with a polite smile as they approached.
"Please, I would like to purchase the ingredients on this list," Kent replied, handing over a detailed list to the seller.
"Well, that is quite a lot. Please, come in; this will take some time," she said, gesturing for them to enter.

Kent and Unity stepped inside the store, where the seller began going through the tall list of ingredients. Shelves lined with jars, bundles of herbs, and vials of strange liquids surrounded them, giving the place a rich, earthy, and herbal aroma.

chapters.title: Chapter 29: Exploring the City
paragraphs: Kent and Unity were offered seats and tea, which Kent accepted with open arms and a grateful smile. He needed a refill, after all. Unity, following his lead, also accepted a cup of tea.
"I have to say, gentleman, this list is rather long," the store owner, Li Zing, remarked, holding the tall list in her hand.
"Well, I need as many of those ingredients as I can get. And you can call me Kent," he replied casually.

"Don’t sweat it, love," Kent replied with a smile. "As for their purity levels, the lowest is 75%, and the highest is 99%," he added, shocking Unity.
"Did you just say you have a 99% pure Tier 0 pill?" Unity asked, her voice tinged with disbelief.
"Four of them, actually," Kent said with a grin. "I’ve got one at 74%, one at 91%, two at 98%, and four at 99%." He didn’t mind bragging a little.
"So, what do you think? Do you know a place where I can sell them?" Kent asked.
"What kind of pills?" Unity questioned again.
"Qi Gathering Pills," Kent answered. Once again, Unity was hit with a wave of astonishment, struggling to process what she had just heard.

And who could blame her? A 75% pure Qi Gathering Pill alone could be used for five hours of cultivation, increasing qi-gathering speed by 30 times. Five hours of absorbing spirit qi at that speed was more than most cultivators could ever dream of.
Unity took a deep breath, trying to calm her surprise. Then she smiled.
"You should sell them at the Silver Leaf Auction House," she said.
Kent raised an eyebrow. "Auction house? Why there?"

"It’s the best place in the city for rare and high-quality items," Unity explained. "The Silver Leaf Auction House is famous for attracting nobles, merchants, and even sect leaders. They bid fiercely for anything valuable."
"Sounds promising," Kent said, nodding.

Unity continued. "The Silver Leaf isn’t just known for its buyers. They also have a special appraisal service. Their appraisers are top-tier. If your pills are as pure as you say, they’ll cause a sensation."
"Anything else I should know?" Kent asked, curious.

"Well," Unity added with a sly smile, "there’s a rumor that the owner of the auction house is a high-ranking cultivator who collects rare treasures. If your pills catch their attention, you might get a personal invitation for their Annual Auction that is coming up in two months"
Kent chuckled. "Now that does sound intriguing. Let’s head there."
Unity nodded, leading the way through the bustling streets toward the grand auction house. They passed by many stores and businesses until they finally stopped in front of a massive building.

Kent stood still for a moment, taking in the sight. The Silver Leaf Auction House was unlike anything he had seen so far. Even his late master hadn’t been there before which makes one wonder if he ever had a life.
Its walls were made of polished white stone that gleamed under the sunlight. Golden patterns ran along the edges, forming intricate designs of leaves and vines.

Two tall pillars framed the entrance, each carved with scenes of legendary battles and treasures. A pair of large wooden doors stood open, their surface adorned with silver inlays shaped like flowing rivers.
Above the entrance, a glowing sign read Silver Leaf Auction House, its letters shining with soft golden light.
The place radiated wealth and power.
"This place is incredible," Kent muttered, his eyes wide.
Unity smiled at his reaction. "Wait until you see the inside. Let’s go."

Kent nodded, still marveling at the grand structure, and followed Unity as they headed in. However, just as they were about to walk through the towering doors, two guards stepped forward, blocking their path.

chapters.title: Chapter 30: Silver Leaf Auction House
paragraphs: Both guards were tall and broad, their polished armor gleaming under the sunlight. They wore matching sneers, their arrogant expressions clearly showing how much they enjoyed their position of authority.

Not that they shouldn’t be arrogant—they were indeed in a good position to be. The Silver Leaf Auction House was a massive establishment, operating in many cities across the kingdom. It wielded considerable authority, and because of this, those who worked there were often prideful.
"Hold it right there," one of them said, his voice gruff. "This isn’t a place for just anyone to walk into."
Unity frowned. "We’re here to sell something valuable," she said firmly. She had visited this auction house on many occasions, but this was the first time she had been stopped from entering.
Of course, she had always been with the Alderford Family during those visits, so she quickly understood why.
At the very least, they should have recognized her. But alas, the Alderford aura hadn’t rubbed off on her.
The second guard chuckled, crossing his arms. "Valuable? That’s what they all say. Do you even have an invitation? Or a recommendation letter? No letter, no entry."
"We are from the Alderford Merchant Family," Unity said, trying to wield the Alderford name as her weapon.
"The Alderford Family?" one of the guards muttered, raising an eyebrow.
"Yes. So you would do well not to block us from entering," Unity added, her tone firm.
"Do you have the Alderford Family emblem," the guard asked, "or anything to prove you’re really from the Alderford Family?"
"No," Unity replied, "but—"
"No buts. No recommendation or invitation, no entry," the guard cut her off before she could finish her sentence.
Kent sighed, glancing at Unity, who looked frustrated. He stepped forward, his tone calm but firm. "We don’t have a letter, but what we have will speak for itself."
The first guard scoffed. "Oh, really? And what’s that?"

Kent smiled faintly, reaching into his ring and pulling out one of his 99% pure Qi Gathering Pills. He held it up between his fingers, letting the sunlight catch its flawless surface. The pill gleamed with an almost ethereal glow, its purity radiating a faint energy that even the guards couldn’t ignore.
The guards froze, their eyes widening as they stared at the pill. The arrogance on their faces quickly faded, replaced by shock and a hint of fear.
"I believe this should be valuable enough," Kent said calmly.
The guards exchanged nervous glances before stepping aside, their previous bravado completely gone. "Go ahead," one of them muttered, his voice suddenly polite.
Kent smiled, slipping the pill back into his ring. "Thank you."
Unity smirked as they walked past the guards into the grand auction house. "Well, that shut them up," she whispered, her tone amused.
Kent chuckled softly. "A little reminder of who they’re dealing with never hurts."

A few seconds after they walked through the huge door, they found themselves inside the auction house in an area that resembled a reception. Kent and Unity were about to make their way to a counter when a lady walked toward them and greeted them.
"Welcome to the Silver Leaf Auction House. I am Manager Alina. How can I assist you today?"
Kent smiled and answered, "I am Kent, an alchemist, and this is my lover, Unity. We are here to sell some pills."
The lady glanced at Unity with a hidden, envious gaze before turning to Kent with a smile. "Thank you for choosing our auction house. Please, how many are you selling, and what is the purity level?"

Kent knew the lady, though she tried to sound polite, didn’t have much faith in him. After all, while it wasn’t a strict requirement to have a high cultivation base to become an alchemist, those with higher cultivation bases tended to make better pills.
Kent was only a Level 6 Root Blossom stage cultivator, so she didn’t have much faith in him. But because of his looks, she held back her arrogance.
"I will be selling 8 Tier 0 pills. One is at 75% purity, another at 91% purity, two more at 95% purity, and four at 99% purity."
Manager Alina’s eyes widened in shock as Kent spoke. Her smile faltered for a moment, and she quickly masked her surprise with a polite expression.
"99% purity...99% purity..." she muttered to herself, processing the numbers. The Tier 0 pills were common, but such high purity levels were rare, especially for someone of Kent’s cultivation.
Kent smiled at her expression and then retrieved the pills.
She glanced at the pills in Kent’s hands, her gaze lingering a little longer than usual. A small flicker of doubt crossed her face—perhaps she had underestimated him.
"These purities... are quite impressive," she said, her tone now more respectful. "Please follow me to the appraisal counter. I’ll have these evaluated right away."
She gestured for them to follow her, her steps a little more careful, her demeanor now more composed. Despite her surprise, she didn’t want to let her guard down completely.

The Silver Leaf Auction House had seen many alchemists, but Kent’s pills were certainly something to be taken seriously. Pills with 99% purity hadn’t appeared in their auction house for the past 16 years.
So, for a pill—even if it was just a Tier 0 Pill—to have such a high purity level, Alina knew she needed to ensure its authenticity.

Her mind raced with possibilities. If Kent’s pills were truly as he claimed, it would be a rare find, and they could fetch an extraordinary price. However, if they turned out to be exaggerated, the reputation of the auction house could be at risk.
She led them to the appraisal counter, where a middle-aged man sat with a serious expression. He glanced up when they approached.
"Manager Alina," he greeted her.
"Please appraise these pills," she said, her voice steady, though a slight edge of urgency lingered. "The purity levels are unusually high. I need your expertise to confirm whether they’re genuine."

The appraiser nodded and carefully took the pills from Kent’s hands, examining them one by one under a magnifying glass. He didn’t speak at first, his focus intense. After a few moments, he nodded again, his eyes widening slightly.
"These are... remarkable," he said, his voice tinged with surprise. "The purity levels are accurate. 75%, 91%, 95% and 99%. These pills are of extraordinary quality for their tier."
Alina’s breath caught, and a rare smile tugged at her lips. Kent’s pills were genuine. This was something special. She turned back to Kent and Unity, her tone now full of respect.
"You weren’t exaggerating. These pills are far beyond what we normally see," she said. "Rest assured, I will handle them with the utmost care."
Kent smiled, but he was much more impressed by the fact that the appraiser had been able to determine the purity after just a few seconds of examining the pills.
’Those are some good senses you have there,’ Kent thought.
[The master can also appraise anything, from women to treasures if he claims his quest’s reward; the Appraiser’s Eye.] The tower chimed in, its voice echoing in his mind.
Kent’s curiosity grew. He hadn’t yet claimed any of his three rewards just yet. But he will soon,
"Master Kent and Lady Unity, kindly follow me to my office," Manager Alina said, breaking his thoughts. She turned and began walking in the direction of her office
Kent and Unity began following her to her office.

chapters.title: Chapter 31: A Nice Offer
paragraphs: The office was rather charming for someone of her nature. Of course, Kent wasn’t focused on that. His eyes wandered over various things as he entered the office.
"Master Kent, once again, thank you for choosing the Silver Leaf Auction House," Manager Alina said. Although the pill was just Tier 0 and not particularly grand, its purity was what intrigued her.

Kent understood this. The pill was quite beneficial for many cultivators. A 75% pure pill could enhance cultivation speed by 30 times for five hours. It wasn’t much, but in the world of cultivation, even a single level-up was something many cherished.

Advancing in cultivation didn’t just bring more power; it also extended one’s lifespan, making even minor progress highly valued. So, despite being a Tier 0 pill, it was still superior to most. Of course, the 91% pure pill would last seven hours and increase speed by 50 times.
A 95% pure pill would work for nine hours, enhancing speed by 55 times, while a 99% pure pill could sustain 24 hours of cultivation at a speed 60 times greater than normal.

This meant that if your normal cultivation speed was already high, the pill would amplify it even further. It was a powerful pill and slightly challenging to concoct, but Kent had pursued it regardless.

Of course, if the tier of the pill were higher, its effects would increase progressively. The same applied if the pill achieved 100% purity, which, in the alchemy world, was referred to as the "perfect pill."
A pill without even an atom of impurity—that was Kent’s ultimate goal.
"No need to be so formal, Manager Alina. Just call me Kent, and I’m happy to be working with your auction house as well," Kent said with a calm smile.
Manager Alina returned his smile and said,

"Although this might sound a bit unofficial, I’d like to purchase your pills personally. Of course, I wouldn’t be paying the standard rate. Since this would be a back-channel purchase, I’d inflate the price by 20% so you could benefit more."
She paused for a moment before continuing, "I would have loved to include these in one of our weekly auctions, but since this week’s auction is nearly over, I’d prefer to buy them directly from you."

"Okay," Kent said without hesitation. He didn’t even need a moment to think it over. He wasn’t particularly fond of the purity level he had achieved anyway. Selling anything less than a perfect pill felt like an insult to his status as an alchemist, so he didn’t mind skipping the auction altogether.
"Really?" Manager Alina was surprised by how casually he accepted her offer.
"I don’t mind you buying them directly from me," Kent said with a gentle smile.
"Thank you," Manager Alina said.
Kent nodded as she pulled out a sheet and began reviewing it. It listed the buying and selling rates for pills traded at the Silver Leaf Auction House.

"According to the auction house’s approved purchase rates," she began, "the 75% pure pill sells for 30 spirit stones, the 91% for 80 spirit stones, the 95% for 100 spirit stones, and the 99% for 150 spirit stones."

He quickly retrieves the last reward he got, a nice card with the name Spirit Stones Multiplier Bingo Card written on it.

sentences.text: "Next item," the auctioneer announced.
"The Azure Frost Blade!
A rare weapon capable of freezing anything it cuts.
Starting bid: 100 Spirit Stones!
Minimum increment: 10 Spirit Stones!"
The hall buzzed with energy.
A man in the regular seating stood up, raising his token high.
"110 Spirit Stones!" he shouted.
Another voice quickly followed, "120 Spirit Stones!" This time, it came from a young woman seated with a group in the corner.
From a VIP room, the number 8 token rose silently.
The auctioneer’s sharp eyes caught it immediately.
"VIP Room 8, 130 Spirit Stones!"
Unity leaned closer to Kent, her voice soft.
"That’s Victor Giln, heir to the Giln Merchant Family.
They control most of the trade routes in Caprath.
Ruthless, but reliable."
Kent nodded, keeping his focus on the bids.
A loud shout interrupted the quiet VIP bidding.
"140 Spirit Stones!" This time it was an older man in the front row, his tone firm.
Unity pointed discreetly to another VIP room as a token with the number 5 rose.
"150 Spirit Stones from VIP Room 5," the auctioneer announced.
"That’s Lady Seraphine, head of the Sylvan Merchant House," Unity murmured.
"She has ties to two of the royal families.
Watch her.
She’s dangerous."
The bids climbed higher as tokens rose in quick succession.
180!" The excitement grew, with voices overlapping and tokens flashing from all corners.
Another silent bid came from the VIP Room 9.
The auctioneer’s voice rang out, "200 Spirit Stones!
VIP Room 2 takes the lead!"
Unity glanced at the room and then back at Kent.
"That’s from the Zarnoth Clan.
They’re not merchants, but they run Caprath’s largest alchemy guild.
Their resources are frightening."
The bids began to slow.
The older man in the front row tried again.
"210 Spirit Stones!" he called out.
But a token rose from VIP Room 8 once more.
"220 Spirit Stones!" the auctioneer announced.
The older man sighed and sat down, shaking his head.
The auctioneer waited for a moment before raising his gavel.
"Going once!
Going twice!
Sold to VIP Room 8 for 220 Spirit Stones!"
Kent remained silent, observing the power plays between the bidders.
Unity smiled softly.
"See how they move?
That’s Caprath’s upper circle, always maneuvering for the best position.
They’ll be useful to know later."
"I guess I would have to rely on you more, my love," Kent said, holding Unity’s hand.
He wasn’t using his skill this time, but he could tell from the way she squeezed his hand that she felt good.
"Then I will do my best to be useful," Unity replied with a blushing smile.
After the dagger was sold, the next item was presented—a Tier 1 pill recipe.
The auctioneer’s voice boomed as he described its details.
"This is a recipe for the Body Strengthening Pill A staple for any alchemist beginning their craft.
Starting bid: 100 Spirit Stones!"
The moment the auction began, the alchemists in the hall came alive.
Voices rang out from the regular seats, and tokens rose from the VIP rooms in rapid succession.
The bids escalated quickly, despite the recipe being for a basic Tier 1 pill.
Kent, however, remained still.
The Tower had already advised him against participating, so he focused on something else instead.
He leaned back and turned his attention inward, bringing up his system interface to review the rewards he had received from completing two recent quests involving Unity.
[Congratulations on completing the quest: Pleasure on the Road.
Your reward is in Tower Storage.]
Kent mentally accessed his Tower Storage, retrieving a cylindrical disc that appeared deceptively ordinary.
Yet, as he held it, he felt the untamed, violent aura that pulsed from within.
[Instant Killing Disc]
[Grade: Heaven]
[Effects:]
- Lethal Strike: Instantly eliminates a target when thrown, as long as the target’s strength does not surpass the user’s by two major realms.
- Return Function: Automatically returns to the user after activation.
- One-Time Recharge: Can be recharged using 5000 Spirit Stones or equivalent energy.
Kent examined the disc with interest.
A tool to instantly kill someone on the same strength level as him or not two major stages above him.
That is a deadly tool.
In situations where he wanted not to raise his sword, he would just throw a disc.
[This tool isn’t that simple Master.
If your soul strength is stronger than your opponent’s, even if they are Three stages above you, it can still kill them.
And the current you can recharge an energy equivalent to 5000 spirit stones within 5 minutes.
So this means you can use it every five minutes]
"Impressive," Kent muttered to himself, smirking.
He could already think of a few ways to use it.
Meanwhile, the sound of escalating bids for the pill recipe continued in the background, drawing him back to the present.
Unity, noticing his slight distraction, leaned closer.
"What is it?" she asked softly.
"Just something new," Kent replied with a smirk, slipping the disc back into storage.
"Something very useful."
Unity nodded, and Kent returned his focus to the Tower Storage, retrieving another item.
This time, it was a skill book.
The title on its cover read [Appraiser’s Eye] in bold, golden lettering.
Without hesitation, Kent tapped the book to his forehead.
A flash of light enveloped him as the knowledge from the book was absorbed directly into his mind.
The book disintegrated into specks of light and vanished.
Unity blinked, clearly startled.
"What did you just do?
Where did the book go?" she asked, her voice filled with curiosity.
Kent smirked.
"I learned the skill directly.
The book was just a medium, and once I absorbed the knowledge, it was no longer needed."
Her eyes widened.
"You mean... you didn’t even have to read it?"
"Exactly.
This husband of yours is no simple person you know" Kent replied casually.
"I know, you have a goddess as your first wife after all" Unity smiled recalling her skepticism when Kent told her about Vexthra.
Looking back the past hour, she would have hated herself if she had continued with her simple thinking of not wanting to tarnish Kent’s image by becoming his woman.
Her life was changed within hours.
Now, she has the means to become her own powerhouse, and for one, she had Kent, the stranger she decided to give her purity to thank.
He glanced at the Tower interface to confirm his new skill.
[Appraiser’s Eye]
[Grade: Rare]
[Rank: SS]
[Effects:]
- Allows the user to analyze the value, origin, and hidden properties of any item with a glance.
It also works on people.
It allows you to see their worth and potential to a certain extent.
- Can detect forgeries and identify true worth.
- Consumes Spiritual qi passively when in use.
Unity tilted her head, intrigued.
"So, what does this skill do?"
"It lets me assess the true nature of items.
No tricks, no forgeries.
Perfect for places like this," Kent explained, gesturing to the auction below.
"Now I can see through anything they bring out here, no matter how well they try to hide its flaws or secrets."
She smiled softly.
"That’s... impressive.
You’ll never get cheated having such a skill."
"That’s the plan," Kent said, smiling.
Now, he wouldn’t have to rely solely on the tower to know some of the important things.
He quickly retrieves the last reward he got, a nice card with the name Spirit Stones Multiplier Bingo Card written on it.

chapters.title: Chapter 34: Spirit Stones Multiplier Bingo Card
paragraphs: The words Spirit Stones Multiplier Bingo Card were neatly inscribed on its surface in elegant, golden letters. Just looking at them exudes luxury and money.
Kent turned the card over in his hand, inspecting it closely. Unity leaned in, curious as ever. "What’s that?" she asked.
"A bingo card, apparently," Kent replied, holding it up so she could see.

He wasn’t worried about Unity knowing some of his secrets. Vexthra had lovingly warned her about some of the dangers and rewards of being with Kent. Essentially, she cautioned her against entertaining any funny ideas.

But that was just Vexthra being overprotective. Kent had no fear of the women he placed the seal on betraying him. While it wasn’t a slave seal, it prevented them from uttering a word of betrayal without catastrophic consequences.

Even without the seal, Vexthra had already ensured that her technique included an additional safeguard. If Unity dared to betray Kent, and the Harem seal somehow failed, her Anti-Betrayal seal would activate.

Essentially, the goddess wanted to ensure that no harm could come from those Kent trusted to be part of him on his journey to the top. She was determined to help him live a good life surrounded by trustworthy lovers.

Unity was now one of them. She belonged to Kent—body, heart, and soul. She wouldn’t betray him, even under threat. Then again, with her sister being a goddess, anyone daring to threaten her would quickly learn the consequences.
"But it’s not just any bingo card. Let me check the details."
[Spirit Stones Multiplier Bingo Card]
[Grade: Legendary]
Effects:]
- Grants the user a chance to multiply Spirit Stones through a game of bingo.
- Each square represents a task or challenge. Completing a row, column, or diagonal activates the multiplier.
- Multiplier varies depending on the number of lines completed, ranging from 2x to 20x.
- Unused after 30 days, the card self-destructs.

Kent raised an eyebrow as he read the description. "Interesting... This could turn out to be extremely useful—or a complete waste, depending on the challenges. But still, 2 times is better than nothing. No lost here"

Unity chuckled softly. "I guess Big Sister Vexthra didn’t say all those things for nothing. You really are a mystery. Makes me wonder what I would’ve done if I’d chickened out when you wanted me to become your woman.
Thank you."

Her gaze reflected genuine emotion, her feelings clear and heartfelt. Unity was indeed very happy at that moment. Her decision to take such a bold step, despite knowing the societal downsides, had proven to be a great one.
"Hey, listen to me. You are now my woman, so I don’t want to see you acting inferior to anyone. You deserve all the love and care now, so be proud instead.

"Plus, I currently don’t have any achievements, so basically, I’m a nobody. But by the time people start to recognize me, you’ll also become a powerhouse. And I doubt that even if people knew your background, they’d dare to mock you.
"But even if they do, it’ll just give me a reason to cut them down," Kent said with a cute smile. Yet Unity knew he meant every single word.
"Then don’t slack off. Make me happy so I can make you happy too," she grinned.
"Oh, I see..." Kent smiled and returned his attention to examining the card. Unity continued to stare at him, lost in thought. Suddenly, a voice entered her head.
< You’re happy now, aren’t you? > Vexthra’s voice spoke, causing Unity’s eyes to widen for a moment.

< Big sister, how are you contacting me? I thought we had already exhausted our five minutes, > Unity asked. The five-minute telepathic connection between her and Vexthra had been used up, so how was she contacting her now?
< I am a goddess, little sis. Although, for some reason, I couldn’t connect with Kent, when I tried it on you, it worked. Now, we can talk all day long. >
< This is good. I guess Kent’s going to love to hear this, > Unity smiled.
< Yeah, but for now, don’t tell him. Let this be our little secret until I figure out a way to include him, > Vexthra said, making Unity nod slightly.
Although she didn’t know how Vexthra managed to contact her, Unity knew she had to trust her, even though keeping such a secret from Kent didn’t sit well with her.

< Don’t worry, Unity. I just need a few days. If it doesn’t work out, you can tell him. Maybe he can take advantage of it. He’s already found a loophole, so I bet he could come up with something too. > Unity smiled, this time genuinely.
At least she wouldn’t have to hold the secret for long.
"You can tell Vexthra I said hi." While Unity was doing her best to hide her expressions so Kent wouldn’t see them, his voice suddenly entered her head, making Unity pale slightly.
< Shit. > Unity transmitted to Vexthra.
< He found out, didn’t he? > Vexthra asked, an amused expression playing on her face as she sat in a hot tub in the god realm.
< Yes... I guess I wasn’t sneaky enough, > Unity said, casting Kent a guilty but cute smile.
"You don’t actually think I wouldn’t notice something like this, do you?" Kent said with a teasing smile.
Just like Vexthra, he had tried using his connection with Unity to tap into her connection with Vexthra to gain some extra minutes, but something was preventing him.
Of course, the Tower had said it was the laws governing the world. This meant that, at his level, he wouldn’t be able to penetrate those laws.

However, he knew Vexthra could, and the only reason she was able to do so was because of the tower tattoo mark under their bellies. Unlike Kent’s women, he didn’t have the tattoo, which was understandable considering he was the one giving them out.

But what he didn’t know was that the moment he added two women to the harem, their souls were linked. Since they both possessed the same essence—the yin essence—so Vexthra used this bond to weave through the laws, giving her direct contact with Unity.
"You are not mad we tried to hide something this important from you?" Unity asked.

"Why would I be? This is a good thing. You can now talk to your sister any day. This also means if I need something, I can just ask you to tell her. It’s a win for me, and since she is a goddess, you can benefit greatly by consulting her on your cultivation.
"So from the way I see it, this would be less work for me teaching you and more time for other things," Kent said with a perverted smile.
Unity leaned in and hugged him. "From me and Big Sister," she muttered before turning away and beginning to converse with Vexthra.
Kent smiled and then decided to focus on the auction. At that moment, another item was sold for 400 spirit stones. Then the next item was brought in.
It was an old sword sheath with no beauty to it, but the moment Kent saw it, thanks to his Appraiser’s Eye skill, he recognized its worth.
He immediately made up his mind to buy this sword sheath no matter what.
